### Two ways to use this page
You’re either looking for a local business in your area — or you’re a local business hoping to be found. And in this economy, more and more people are both: a customer in their own neighborhood by day, a side-gig owner serving the next town over by night. We built this directory to serve both sides of that equation, in every city we cover.
Pick the side that fits where you stand today.

Looking for a Business

### Find the right business in your city, your town, or your neighborhood.
We cover 1,340+ Missouri and Illinois cities and towns — from Maryland Heights, Clayton, Webster Groves, Chesterfield, St. Charles, O’Fallon, St. Peters, Kirkwood, and Ballwin on the Missouri side; to Belleville, Edwardsville, Glen Carbon, and Collinsville on the Illinois side. We even cover the small ones — Alton, Illinois and Eureka, Missouri are in here too.
Type your city or town in the search box above to filter the list. Click through to discover the thousands of businesses serving your area — every one reviewed by a human before going live, so you don’t waste time on zombie listings or fake bot profiles.
Browsing is 100% free with no signup required. A free user account (30 seconds, no payment) lets you message businesses directly, save favorites, and comment on posts.
Looking by service type instead of by place?
Browse by Category Free Account

Running a Business

### One listing. Up to 40 of the cities you actually serve.
Most directories make you choose one city — and then charge extra for every additional location. We don’t. A single listing reaches up to 40 of the cities and towns you actually serve , so the plumber based in Maryland Heights who covers Webster Groves, Kirkwood, and Clayton shows up in all four searches without paying four times.
Membership starts at less than $1 a day. Every plan includes a schema-optimized profile, multi-location and service-area visibility, photos, videos, blogs, products, services, coupons, events, jobs, and review management — all wired into the right city pages so customers find you when they search “tattoo Maryland Heights” or “dentist Edwardsville.”
Paid plans add AI-powered Google Business Profile optimization, social media posting, citation building, and review management through our AI assistant Mara — so the work happens whether you have time to log in or not.
Not sure where your business currently stands online? Run a free 90-second audit before deciding anything.
Run a Free Audit Compare Plans

Whichever side you’re on today — thanks for being here. Every city and town on this list has good businesses doing real work, and we built this so neither of you have to do the finding the hard way.

### Service-Area Business FAQs

### Can a business with no storefront still rank in local search?
Absolutely. Service-area businesses rank with a properly configured Google Business Profile — address hidden, service area defined — plus reviews, citations, and content that signal the communities you cover. You don’t need a storefront to win “near me” searches.

### Should I hide my home address on Google?
Yes, if you serve customers at their location rather than yours. Google lets service-area businesses hide the address and show a service area instead — that’s the correct, penalty-safe setup for a home-based business.

### How many areas can I list?
Google allows roughly 20 service areas on a profile, so we prioritize the communities that matter most to you and reinforce them with citations and content.

### Can I rank in multiple suburbs at once?
Yes — that’s the goal for a service-area business. With the right service-area setup, local content, and citations, you can be found across every community you serve rather than just where you happen to live.

### Is it against the rules to list a fake address for more coverage?
Yes, and it’s risky — fake addresses and lister-only locations are a common cause of profile suspension. We only use legitimate, policy-safe service-area setups.

### How much does service-area marketing cost?
Our plans start at less than a dollar a day and scale as you grow, so a home-based business gets a real local presence without an agency-sized retainer.

### Q. What areas does St Louis Near Me Directory cover?
A.  St Louis Near Me Directory covers the entire greater St. Louis metro — St. Louis City, St. Louis County, St. Charles, Jefferson, and Franklin counties, and additional Missouri counties — plus the Metro East communities on the Illinois side. Its tools and support also help businesses across Missouri and Illinois beyond the metro.

### Q. Does the directory cover the Illinois side of St. Louis?
A.  Yes. St Louis Near Me Directory covers the Metro East — the Illinois communities across the river, such as Belleville, Edwardsville, O’Fallon IL, Granite City, and Alton — alongside the Missouri metro, so businesses and customers on both sides of the river are included.

### Q. Does St Louis Near Me Directory cover my county?
A.  The directory serves St. Louis City and County, St. Charles County, Jefferson County, Franklin County, and additional Missouri counties, plus the Illinois Metro East. If you’re anywhere in the greater St. Louis region — or across Missouri and Illinois — search the directory or reach out to confirm coverage for your area.

### Q. Is the directory only for the St. Louis metro?
A.  The core coverage is the St. Louis metro, but St Louis Near Me Directory’s tools and process help local businesses get found across Missouri and Illinois — not only in the metro. Businesses in communities well beyond St. Louis use it to improve their local visibility.

### Q. How do I add my Missouri business to the directory?
A.  Create a listing to put your business on the map and in front of local customers searching across the region. A complete, consistent profile is one of the highest-return, lowest-cost ways to get found on Google, Maps, and AI search — visit the join page to get started, and the Gold Plan adds premium placement.

### Q. Is a coverage map pin enough to showcase my business?
A.  A pin shows where you serve, but it carries only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives you a rich description, photos, services, offers, and reviews, plus category placement — far more than a pin alone can do to bring you local customers.

### Every location is its own ranking battle
Run two, five, or twenty locations and you don’t have one Google Business Profile — you have one for each , and every one competes in its own map pack against its own local rivals. Keeping them all complete, consistent, and active is a real job, and when it slips, whole locations go quiet.
Multi-location profile management keeps every location optimized and on-brand — without losing the local nuance that makes each one rank.

### What Multi-Location Management Includes
Consistency at scale, local relevance at each pin:

### Per-Location Optimization
Each profile fully optimized for its own city, categories, and service area — not copy-pasted.

### NAP Consistency
Name, address, and phone correct and uniform across every location and every citation.

### Reviews by Location
Review generation and replies handled location by location, where they actually count.

### Location-Level Posts
Offers and updates tailored to each location’s market, on a steady cadence.

### Centralized Oversight
One team watching every profile, so nothing falls through the cracks at any location.

### Local Landing Pages
City-specific pages that reinforce each location — like our 30 city SEO pages .

### Consistent and Local — Not One or the Other
The trap with multiple locations is going too far in one direction: either every profile looks identical (and none rank locally), or each is a mess with no brand consistency. The win is both — uniform NAP and branding, with genuinely local categories, reviews, and content at each pin. That balance is exactly what we manage.
It’s the multi-location version of full Google Business Profile management , backed by our Local SEO hub .

### Multi-Location GBP FAQs

### How is managing multiple Google profiles different from one?
Each location is a separate profile competing in its own local map pack, so the work multiplies — per-location optimization, reviews, posts, and citations — while branding and accuracy have to stay consistent across all of them. It needs a system, not ad-hoc edits.

### Should every location have its own profile?
Yes — each staffed location with its own address should have its own Google Business Profile. That’s how each one becomes eligible to rank for its own neighborhood and suburb.

### How do you keep all the locations consistent?
With standardized name, address, phone, and branding across every profile and citation, managed centrally — while still tailoring categories, reviews, and posts to each location’s local market.

### Can you handle reviews for each location separately?
Yes. Review generation and responses are handled location by location, because reviews rank and convert at the location level, not the brand level.

### Do multi-location businesses need local landing pages too?
They help a lot. A dedicated, city-specific page per location reinforces relevance and gives each profile something local to point to — the same approach behind our 30 city SEO pages.

### How much does multi-location management cost?
It scales with the number of locations, but our plans start at less than a dollar a day per location and grow with you — far below a traditional multi-location agency retainer.

### Directory Listings FAQs

### What are local citations and why do they matter?
A citation is any online mention of your business name, address, and phone. Consistent citations across the web tell Google and AI that your business is real and established, which is a foundational local ranking signal.

### Does my business need to be on a lot of directories?
Quality and consistency matter more than sheer quantity. Being accurately listed on the directories that feed Google and AI — with identical details — beats being on hundreds with sloppy information.

### What is NAP consistency?
NAP stands for Name, Address, Phone. NAP consistency means those details are identical everywhere you’re listed. Inconsistencies (old addresses, different phone numbers) confuse search engines and hurt your ranking.

### Can inconsistent listings actually hurt me?
Yes. Conflicting or duplicate listings make Google less confident about your business, which can suppress your map-pack visibility. Cleaning them up is often a quick, meaningful win.

### Is a directory listing the same as a backlink?
They overlap — a good directory listing is both a citation and often a link, which supports local trust and SEO at once.

### How much does listings management cost?
Our plans start at less than a dollar a day and scale as you grow, so you get consistent citations and ongoing accuracy without an agency-sized retainer.

### How much does painting cost in St. Louis?
Interior work is usually priced per square foot or per room; exterior by the size of the home. Typical 2026 ranges:
Painting job Typical cost
Interior (per sq ft) $2–$6 per sq ft
Interior (per room) $300–$1,000 per room
Whole-house interior $1,800–$12,000 (most spend $4,200–$9,500)
Exterior house $3,500–$9,000 (2,000 sq ft, two-story)
Kitchen cabinets $30–$70 per linear foot
Paint (per gallon) $20–$100+ (labor is 60–85% of the job)

National 2026 estimates (Angi, HomeGuide); St. Louis labor typically lands in the lower half of these ranges. Get an itemized written estimate.

### The one thing to check before hiring a St. Louis painter
Missouri and St. Louis do not license painters as a trade — but there is a federal rule that matters enormously here. Any firm paid to disturb paint in a home built before 1978 must be EPA Lead-Safe Certified (the Renovation, Repair and Painting, or RRP, rule). Nearly 90% of housing in the City of St. Louis was built before 1978 , so this is not a technicality — sanding or scraping old lead paint without containment is how lead dust poisons a household, and the EPA has penalized St. Louis-area renovators for violations. Ask for the firm’s EPA Lead-Safe certification, or check the EPA’s certified-firm search or the lead hotline at 1-800-424-LEAD before interior prep work begins.

### Painting St. Louis brick and old plaster
Two local realities shape the work. St. Louis’s signature brick homes need breathable masonry paint and fully dry walls — trapping moisture in the pores causes peeling and blistering, and painting brick is largely a one-way decision. Inside, the region’s older homes have plaster walls that behave differently from modern drywall and need more prep. And because St. Louis summers are humid, exterior painting goes best in spring and fall, when paint cures properly instead of trapping moisture on a muggy 90-degree afternoon.

### FAQ – St Louis Painting Contractors Near You

### Q. How much does it cost to paint the inside of a 1500 sq ft house?
A.  Painting the interior of a roughly 1,500-square-foot St. Louis home typically runs about $3,000 to $7,500, depending on how many rooms, ceilings, and trim are included and the wall condition. Figured another way, interior painting runs about $2 to $6 per square foot of floor area. Older homes with plaster walls that need patching sit toward the higher end.

### Q. How much is labor to paint the interior of a house?
A.  Labor is the biggest piece — roughly 60% to 85% of an interior paint job’s total cost. Painters in the St. Louis area generally charge about $25 to $75 an hour, or price by the room or square foot. That’s why prep-heavy old homes cost more: the labor to patch plaster, sand, and mask takes longer than the painting itself.

### Q. What time of year is best to paint a house?
A.  For exterior painting in St. Louis, late spring and early fall are ideal — mild temperatures and moderate humidity let the paint cure properly. Summer’s heat and humidity can trap moisture and slow drying, and winter is usually too cold for exterior coatings. Interior painting can be done any time of year, though opening windows is easier in the shoulder seasons.

### Q. How much does it cost to paint a full house interior?
A.  A full interior repaint in St. Louis typically runs $1,800 to $12,000, with most homeowners spending about $4,200 to $9,500 for a roughly 2,000-square-foot home including walls, ceilings, and trim. The spread depends on square footage, the number of colors, trim and ceiling work, and how much prep the walls need. Always get an itemized written estimate.

### Q. Is it cheaper to spray or roll paint?
A.  Spraying is faster and usually cheaper on labor for large, open, or exterior surfaces, while rolling gives a thicker, more durable finish and far less masking on detailed interiors. Many St. Louis pros combine them — spray-and-back-roll — for coverage plus adhesion. On an older home with lots of trim and old paint, rolling and brushing often wins on quality.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my painting business?
A.  Map pins show where you work, but they carry only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives you room for a rich description, a portfolio of photos, services, offers, and reviews, plus category placement — far more than a pin alone. See how we’re different, and our Gold Plan puts your painting business in front of more local customers.

### How much does pest control cost in St. Louis?
Most homeowners pay a one-time visit fee or a recurring plan; big infestations are priced separately. Typical 2026 ranges:
Pest-control service Typical cost
General pest — one-time visit $100–$260 (about $171 average)
General pest — recurring plan $40–$80 per month (quarterly plans common)
Termite treatment (+ inspection) $225–$2,500 per treatment
Bed bug treatment $1,000–$4,000 whole-home
Mosquito treatment $80–$150 per visit ($350–$1,000 seasonal)
Rodent / mice removal $150–$600

National 2026 estimates (Angi, HomeGuide); St. Louis typically falls within these ranges. Recurring plans usually cost less per visit than one-time calls.

### Is pest control licensed in Missouri? (Yes — verify it)
Unlike many home-service trades, pest control is regulated. In Missouri, any company applying pesticides for hire must hold a Pesticide Business License from the Missouri Department of Agriculture and employ a Certified Commercial Applicator who has passed the state exam. That makes “ask for their Missouri Department of Agriculture license” a concrete way to separate a legitimate exterminator from an unlicensed sprayer — you can confirm a company’s certification by calling the MDA Pesticide Control Program at 573-751-5504 . (Illinois Metro East companies are licensed separately, through the Illinois Department of Public Health.)

### The pests St. Louis homes actually face
Three local realities drive most calls. Brown recluse spiders are documented statewide in Missouri and are frequently found indoors in dry, cluttered, undisturbed spaces — though University of Missouri researchers note bites are rare and roughly 90% heal on their own, so the fearsome reputation is overstated. Subterranean termites thrive in the region’s humid summers, moisture-holding clay soil, and older wood-framed housing, entering through mud tubes — which is why an annual inspection is the standard defense. And mice exploit the foundation gaps and old plumbing penetrations of St. Louis’s aging brick homes, especially as it cools off in fall.

### FAQ – St Louis Pest Control Near You

### Q. What is the hardest pest to get rid of?
A.  Bed bugs and German cockroaches are widely considered the hardest, because they hide in tiny cracks, breed fast, and often survive a single treatment — which is why bed bug jobs run $1,000 to $4,000 and usually need follow-up visits. In St. Louis, subterranean termites are the most stubborn structural pest, since the colony lives underground and requires professional barrier or bait treatment.

### Q. How much is a full house pest control?
A.  A one-time whole-house general pest treatment in St. Louis typically runs about $100 to $260 (roughly $171 on average), scaling with home size. Most companies then offer a recurring plan at about $40 to $80 a month or a quarterly visit, which usually costs less per treatment and includes free re-service between visits if pests return.

### Q. What is the average cost of pest control in my area?
A.  In the St. Louis metro, expect about $100 to $260 for a one-time general treatment and $40 to $80 a month for an ongoing plan. Specialty jobs cost more: termites $225 to $2,500, bed bugs $1,000 to $4,000, and mosquito service $80 to $150 a visit. Home size, pest type, and severity move the final price.

### Q. What pest is most damaging to a house?
A.  Termites, by far. Subterranean termites quietly eat structural wood from the inside and cause billions in U.S. damage a year, and St. Louis’s humid climate and clay soil put local homes squarely in their range. Because the damage is hidden, an annual termite inspection — and treating at the first sign of mud tubes — is the cheapest protection you can buy.

### Q. What time of year is best for pest control?
A.  Early spring is ideal: treating before pests become active knocks down colonies as they emerge and heads off summer infestations. That said, St. Louis benefits from year-round or quarterly service — mosquitoes and ants peak in summer, rodents move indoors in fall, and brown recluse spiders are active in warm months — so a recurring plan protects better than a single seasonal spray.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my pest-control business?
A.  Map pins show where you work, but they carry only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives you room for a rich description, your licensing and credentials, services, offers, and reviews, plus category placement — far more than a pin alone. See how we’re different, and our Gold Plan puts your pest-control business in front of more local customers.

### What’s licensed in Missouri — and what isn’t
This is the most useful thing to know before you book: not every pet service is regulated the same way.
Service Licensed in Missouri? What to verify
Groomers No — not state-licensed NDGAA certification, insurance, a facility tour, vaccine rules
Boarding / kennels / daycare Yes — MO Dept. of Agriculture (ACFA), inspected yearly Current ACFA license and inspection history
Veterinarians Yes — MO Veterinary Medical Board License on the MO PRO public lookup

Because Missouri does not license groomers, you have to vet them yourself — look for NDGAA certification, proof of insurance, a clean facility you can tour, and clear vaccination requirements (reputable groomers, boarders, and daycares require proof, not just your word). Boarding facilities are licensed and inspected by the Missouri Department of Agriculture, so you can confirm a kennel’s license status directly.

### St. Louis pet-care realities
The metro is full of excellent independent groomers, boarders, daycares, and mobile services — and a few local realities are worth planning around. Missouri sits in a heightened heartworm and tick-borne-disease corridor along the Mississippi (per the Companion Animal Parasite Council), so year-round prevention matters here. St. Louis summers get dangerously hot — never leave a pet in a parked car — and holiday boarding fills up fast, so book early.

### Before you need it: know your emergency vet
The best time to find a 24/7 emergency animal hospital is before an emergency. The metro has round-the-clock emergency and specialty vets — identify your nearest one now and keep the number on the fridge, alongside your regular vet and a trusted pet sitter.

### FAQ – St Louis Pet Services Near You

### Q. How much does dog grooming cost in St. Louis?
A.  A full groom in St. Louis typically runs $30 to $75 for a small breed and $90 to $140 for a large breed, depending on coat and condition. Mobile grooming adds roughly 10 to 30 percent over a salon. Ask each groomer for a quote based on your dog’s size and coat.

### Q. How much does dog boarding cost in St. Louis?
A.  Overnight dog boarding in the St. Louis area generally runs $25 to $85 per night, with basic kennels at the lower end and pet resorts higher. Doggy daycare is about $18 to $30 a day. Holiday weeks book up fast, so reserve early and confirm vaccine requirements.

### Q. Are dog groomers licensed in Missouri?
A.  No. Missouri does not license or regulate pet groomers, so there’s no state credential floor — you vet them yourself. Look for NDGAA certification, proof of insurance, a clean facility you can tour, and clear vaccination requirements. Boarding kennels, by contrast, are licensed and inspected by the Missouri Department of Agriculture.

### Q. What are the red flags for dog grooming?
A.  Watch for a groomer who won’t let you tour the facility, gets defensive about their policies, doesn’t require proof of vaccination, or can’t show insurance or certification. Since Missouri doesn’t license groomers, those signals are how you separate a professional from a risk to your pet.

### Q. How do I choose a good boarding facility in St. Louis?
A.  Confirm the kennel holds a current Missouri Department of Agriculture (ACFA) license and passes yearly inspection, then tour it: look for clean, climate-controlled spaces, required vaccinations, clear emergency-vet procedures, and staff on-site overnight. Book early around holidays, when St. Louis boarders fill up.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my pet-services business?
A.  Map pins show where you work, but they carry only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives you room for a rich description, photos, services, offers, and reviews, plus category placement — far more than a pin alone. ### Plumbing Services Available

### How much does a plumber cost in St. Louis?
Most St. Louis plumbers charge roughly $80 to $200 an hour , and the typical repair job runs around $292 . Bigger jobs are priced by scope, not the clock. Here are realistic 2026 ranges so you can spot a fair quote:
Plumbing job Typical St. Louis cost
Service / diagnostic call $80–$575 (average job ~$292)
Hourly rate $80–$200 per hour
Clear a clogged drain $50–$450 (main line up to ~$1,000)
Water heater replacement (50-gal tank) $1,300–$1,900 installed
Main sewer line repair / replacement $3,500–$15,000
Sump pump replacement ~$400–$1,200 (national estimate)

Ranges are typical 2026 estimates (Angi, HomeBlue); your actual quote depends on the job, access, and after-hours timing. Always get an itemized written estimate before work begins.

### Do you need a licensed plumber in St. Louis?
Here’s what surprises most people: Missouri has no statewide plumber’s license. Plumbers are licensed locally, and St. Louis City and St. Louis County each run their own boards — a license in one does not authorize work in the other. So “licensed in St. Louis” isn’t specific enough; confirm your plumber is licensed in your jurisdiction (the City, the County, or your municipality).
To verify: St. Louis County publishes public lists of licensed Master Plumbers and Drainlayers (License Office 314-615-3741 ), and the City’s Plumbing Section is 314-622-3313 . Only a Master Plumber — or a Master Drainlayer for sewer work — can pull the permit, and nearly all plumbing beyond a like-for-like faucet or disposal swap requires one.

### St. Louis plumbing problems worth knowing about
Your sewer lateral is your responsibility — but there’s help. The lateral line connecting your home to the public sewer is the homeowner’s to maintain, and in St. Louis’s older neighborhoods those lines fail. Both the City and the County run repair programs funded by a small property-tax fee:
Program Cost What it covers
City of St. Louis lateral program ~$28/yr on property taxes Repair of a broken lateral under the public right-of-way
St. Louis County lateral program ~$28/yr on property taxes County arranges repair of a qualifying broken lateral
Your municipality Varies Many cities (Maplewood, Florissant, Bridgeton…) run their own — check yours

Important: these programs pay to repair a broken or collapsed lateral — they do not cover routine clog or tree-root clearing, which stays the homeowner’s job. Your property taxes must be current to qualify, and coverage varies by jurisdiction, so confirm your own city’s rules.
Old pipes and roots. St. Louis’s older housing stock means aging galvanized and cast-iron supply lines that corrode, plus clay and Orangeburg (fiber) sewer laterals from the mid-1900s that crack at the joints and invite tree roots. If your home is pre-1970 and the lateral has never been scoped, a camera inspection is cheap insurance.
Hard water. The metro has moderately hard water — Missouri American Water reports roughly 4 to 13 grains per gallon for the region — which builds scale that shortens water-heater and fixture life. A softener and a periodic water-heater flush pay for themselves. And every Missouri winter brings freeze-thaw swings that burst unprotected pipes, so insulate exposed lines and disconnect hoses before the first hard freeze.

### When to call an emergency plumber
Some problems can’t wait. A burst pipe, a sewage backup, no water, or a gas smell is an emergency: shut off your water main (or gas) and call a 24/7 plumber — round-the-clock service is standard across the metro. One tip that saves money and surprises: nights, weekends, and holidays often carry an after-hours premium, so ask about it upfront when you call.

### FAQ – St Louis Plumbers Near You

### Q. How much do plumbers charge per hour in St. Louis?
A.  Most St. Louis plumbers charge about $80 to $200 per hour, and the typical repair runs around $292. Clearing a drain often costs $50 to $450, a tank water-heater replacement about $1,300 to $1,900 installed, and a main sewer line repair anywhere from $3,500 to $15,000. Always get an itemized written estimate.

### Q. Do I need a licensed plumber in St. Louis?
A.  For anything beyond a simple faucet or disposal swap, yes. Missouri has no statewide plumber license — St. Louis City and County each license separately, and a license in one does not cover the other. Confirm your plumber is licensed in your jurisdiction and can pull the permit. Verify with St. Louis County (314-615-3741) or the City (314-622-3313).

### Q. Who is responsible for repairing my sewer lateral in St. Louis?
A.  The homeowner owns the sewer lateral. Both the City and St. Louis County run programs — about $28 a year on your property taxes — that help pay to repair a broken lateral in the public right-of-way, but they do not cover routine clog or tree-root clearing. Many municipalities run their own programs, so check your city’s rules.

### Q. How do I find a good plumber in St. Louis?
A.  Start with the map above, then confirm the plumber is licensed and insured in your jurisdiction, read recent reviews, and get two or three itemized written estimates for the same scope. Ask whether pricing is flat-rate or hourly, whether they’ll pull the required permit, and whether after-hours work carries a premium.

### Q. How do I know if I’m overpaying a plumber?
A.  Get two or three written quotes for the same job and compare line items, not just totals. Be cautious of anyone who won’t itemize, insists on cash only, skips the permit, or pressures you to decide on the spot. A fair St. Louis plumber will explain the work, quote it in writing, and stand behind it.

### Q. What is the most common plumbing repair?
A.  The everyday calls are clogged drains, running or leaking toilets, dripping faucets, and water-heater trouble. In older St. Louis homes, aging galvanized supply lines and cracked clay or Orangeburg sewer laterals — often invaded by tree roots — are common bigger-ticket repairs worth catching early with a camera inspection.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my plumbing business?
A.  Map pins are helpful for showing where a business serves, but they only allow limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives room for richer descriptions, photos, offers, reviews, and category placement, so relying only on a map pin would short-change your visibility compared to what a complete directory profile can do.

### How much does a roof cost in St. Louis?
A full roof replacement in St. Louis averages around $8,155 , with most homes landing between $5,433 and $11,032. A typical 2,000-square-foot home with architectural asphalt shingles runs roughly $8,500–$14,500. Ranges to expect:
Roofing job Typical St. Louis cost
Full replacement (average) ~$8,155 (most $5,433–$11,032)
2,000 sq ft, architectural asphalt ~$8,500–$14,500
Asphalt shingles, installed ~$4.00–$6.50 per sq ft
Tear-off & disposal $1–$5 per sq ft (~$1,000–$2,500)

Ranges as reported by Angi (St. Louis) and local roofers; hail damage, pitch, and materials all affect the final price. Get an itemized written estimate.

### Roofers, hail, and the St. Louis storm-chaser problem
Here’s the fact that protects you most: Missouri does not license roofers at the state level. That low barrier is exactly why out-of-town “storm chasers” flood the metro after a hail event — and St. Louis is genuinely hail-prone, ranking among the hardest-hit U.S. metros most years. The Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance has issued consumer alerts about post-storm contractor fraud; its consumer hotline is 800-726-7390 . Protect yourself: hire a local, permanently-based, insured roofer with references, never pay large sums up front, and get everything in writing.

### Roof insurance claims: know the Missouri law
After hail or wind damage, document everything with photos and get a licensed local roofer to inspect before you file. And know this: in Missouri it is illegal for a contractor to waive or rebate your insurance deductible as a sales pitch (RSMo 407.725). Anyone offering to “eat your deductible” is a red flag — it can expose both of you to fraud. Missouri law also gives you a five-business-day right to cancel a storm-repair contract after your insurer notifies you a claim isn’t covered.

### What St. Louis weather does to a roof
Beyond hail, St. Louis roofs take a beating from high winds, and winter freeze-thaw cycles that can lift shingles and drive ice dams at the eaves. Combined with the metro’s older housing stock, that means an annual look — and a professional inspection after any major storm — pays for itself by catching small problems before they reach the decking.

### Why Choose Local St. Louis Roofers?
✓  Licensed & Insured - Fully qualified roofing contractors ✓  Storm Experience - Familiar with St Louis weather and storm damage ✓  Quality Materials - Premium roofing products and warranties ✓ Local Reputation - Trusted contractors serving your community

### FAQ – St Louis Roofers Near You

### Q. How much does it cost to replace a roof in St. Louis?
A.  A full roof replacement in St. Louis averages about $8,155, with most homes between $5,433 and $11,032. A typical 2,000-square-foot home with architectural asphalt shingles runs roughly $8,500 to $14,500. Hail damage, roof pitch, and material choice all affect the final number, so get an itemized written estimate.

### Q. How much does it cost to shingle a 2,000 sq ft roof in St. Louis?
A.  Expect roughly $8,500 to $14,500 for a 2,000-square-foot St. Louis home in architectural asphalt shingles, or about $4.00 to $6.50 per square foot installed. Tear-off and disposal of the old roof typically adds $1 to $5 per square foot.

### Q. Can a roofer waive my insurance deductible in Missouri?
A.  No. Under Missouri law (RSMo 407.725) it is illegal for a contractor to waive or rebate your insurance deductible as an inducement to sign. Treat any “we’ll cover your deductible” offer as a red flag — it can expose both you and the contractor to fraud.

### Q. How do I avoid a bad roofer in St. Louis?
A.  Because Missouri doesn’t license roofers, vet them yourself: hire a local, permanently-based company with proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp, check references and reviews, never pay large sums up front, and get everything in writing. Be wary of door-knocking storm chasers after a hail event.

### Q. Do I need a permit to replace my roof in St. Louis?
A.  Usually yes. The City of St. Louis requires a permit when a re-roof isn’t a like-for-like replacement or when more than 25% of the sheathing is replaced, and most St. Louis County municipalities require a permit for full replacements. Your licensed roofer should handle it — confirm with the Building Division for your jurisdiction.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my roofing business?
A.  Map pins show where you work, but they carry only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives you room for a rich description, photos, services, offers, and reviews, plus category placement — far more than a pin alone. See how we’re different, and our Gold Plan puts your roofing business in front of more local customers.

### Top-rated St. Louis-area school districts
Ladue is consistently ranked the St. Louis area’s top public district — named among the top 10 school districts in the country in the 2026 Niche cycle — and Ladue Horton Watkins High is rated the area’s #1 public high school. Clayton ranks just behind (around 31st nationally), with Clayton High rated #2 in the metro. Other consistently high-performing districts include Kirkwood, Rockwood, Parkway, Lindbergh, and Webster Groves (Rockwood and Parkway are also among the metro’s largest). Missouri rates districts through the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education’s Annual Performance Report under the Missouri School Improvement Program (MSIP 6), and DESE reports that more than 90% of Missouri public schools meet or exceed state standards. For the current, full ranked list, compare districts on Niche and on DESE’s report cards — rankings shift year to year.

### How to choose and compare St. Louis schools
For traditional public schools, your address sets your district and assigned school, so families often shop for a home and a school together. Inside the city, SLPS magnet schools admit by a city-wide lottery with applications typically due in the fall. The long-running VICC city-to-county transfer program is winding down — it stopped enrolling new students starting in 2024–25, though students already enrolled may continue. To compare options, use GreatSchools ratings and MO DESE’s report cards for Missouri schools, and the Illinois Report Card for Metro East districts such as Edwardsville, O’Fallon, and Belleville. One current note for city families: in January 2026 the Missouri state board voted 6–1 to move St. Louis Public Schools to provisionally accredited , citing leadership, transportation, and finance issues outside the academic scoring formula; the district continues to operate, graduate students, and employ staff normally.

### How is local SEO different from regular SEO?

### How long does SEO take to work?

### How much do spa services cost in St. Louis?
St. Louis spa pricing tracks the national Midwest band, with luxury hotel spas at the top. Typical 2026 ranges:
Spa service Typical St. Louis cost
60-minute massage $70–$120 (luxury hotel spas $160+)
90-minute massage ~$95–$195
Basic facial $70–$130
Spa day package $150–$320
Botox (med spa) $10–$20 per unit ($350–$900 per treatment)

Ranges from St. Louis spa menus and national cost guides; spa menus change, so confirm current pricing when you book.

### Is your St. Louis spa properly licensed?
This is the part worth checking before you lie down on the table. In Missouri, massage therapists must be licensed by the Board of Therapeutic Massage, and estheticians must be licensed by the Board of Cosmetology — and you can verify any practitioner by name on the state’s public license lookup at mopro.mo.gov . Here’s who does what:
Type What they do Licensed / oversight
Day spa Massage, facials, body treatments, nails — non-medical Licensed LMTs & estheticians
Med spa Injectables (Botox/filler), laser — medical procedures Must have a physician medical director
Salon Hair, nails, basic skin care Licensed cosmetologists

The line that matters most: injectables and laser are the practice of medicine in Missouri and must be done by, or delegated by, a licensed physician — a legitimate med spa has a named medical director with an MD, NP, or PA overseeing treatments. A 2025 study found many Missouri med spas fall short on that oversight, so it’s a fair question to ask before any injectable.

### How to pick a spa (and what to avoid)
A few minutes of homework saves a bad experience. Look up your massage therapist or esthetician by name at mopro.mo.gov, look for posted licenses and a clean, sanitary space, and read recent third-party reviews. Packages (a day pass plus a service or two) usually beat à-la-carte pricing, and weekends and holidays book up, so reserve early. Walk away from any practitioner you can’t find on the license search, any med spa offering injectables with no named medical director, and high-pressure membership sales at the table.

### FAQ – St Louis Day Spas Near You

### Q. How much does a massage cost in St. Louis?
A.  A 60-minute massage in St. Louis typically runs $70 to $120, with luxury hotel spas at $160 and up. A 90-minute massage is roughly $95 to $195. Packages and memberships lower the per-session price, so ask — and confirm current rates when you book, since spa menus change.

### Q. How much does a spa day cost in St. Louis?
A.  A St. Louis spa day package generally runs $150 to $320 depending on how many services are included — a day pass plus a massage or facial sits at the lower end, while multi-service packages reach the top. Buying a package is usually better value than booking each service separately.

### Q. What is the difference between a day spa and a med spa?
A.  A day spa offers non-medical relaxation and beauty services — massage, facials, body treatments — staffed by licensed massage therapists and estheticians. A med spa also performs medical procedures like Botox, fillers, and laser, which in Missouri require a physician medical director overseeing treatment. If a spa offers injectables, confirm who that doctor is.

### Q. Are massage therapists licensed in Missouri?
A.  Yes. Missouri requires massage therapists to be licensed by the state Board of Therapeutic Massage, and estheticians by the Board of Cosmetology. You can verify any practitioner by name on the state’s public license lookup at mopro.mo.gov. If someone isn’t listed, don’t book.

### Q. Are med spas safe in Missouri?
A.  They can be, if properly run. Injectables and laser are the practice of medicine in Missouri and must be performed or delegated by a licensed physician, so a safe med spa has a named medical director with an MD, NP, or PA overseeing care. A 2025 study found many Missouri med spas lack adequate oversight — so ask who the medical director is before any treatment.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my spa business?
A.  Map pins show where you work, but they carry only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives you room for a rich description, photos, services, offers, and reviews, plus category placement — far more than a pin alone. ### Mark Twain I-70 Industrial Businesses & Neighborhood Guide | St Louis Near Me Directory
Mark Twain I-70 Industrial, St. Louis
Mark Twain I-70 Industrial is a working freight-and-industrial corridor in north St. Louis, wedged between Interstate 70 and Natural Bridge Road. It is a distinct place from the residential Mark Twain neighborhood next door — same name, different job: this corridor is built for warehousing, contracting, and freight, not for browsing or dining, and the businesses that operate here reflect that.
Mark Twain I-70 Industrial sits in north St. Louis at approximately 38.6875° N, 90.2714° W , within zip code 63120. The corridor is framed by Interstate 70 on the north and Natural Bridge Road on the south, with North Kingshighway and West Florissant Avenue forming the primary east-west arteries. The district shares its name and freight-corridor location with the adjacent Mark Twain residential neighborhood, but it is a separate place built for industry rather than housing — the industrial-and-logistics backbone connecting north St. Louis to downtown, Lambert Airport, and the Illinois side via the I-70 / I-44 / I-64 gateway.
The corridor’s cornerstone is the Union 70 Center , a major industrial hub bounded by Interstate 70 and Natural Bridge Road. As the central component of the area’s commercial infrastructure, the center provides extensive warehouse and distribution space designed for large-scale logistics and manufacturing tenants, with immediate access to I-70 for regional freight movement. Local planning has targeted the corridor for continued industrial investment, and Union 70 remains the anchor around which the rest of the district’s trade and contracting businesses operate.
Beyond Union 70 Center’s warehouse space, the corridor’s working businesses are almost entirely trade and logistics operations. Best One of St. Louis , listed on Google as Best-One Tire & Service, keeps commercial fleets and trucks rolling on Brown Avenue. NextGen Roofing and Building Technology handle roofing and general contracting work out of Union Boulevard and North Riverview Boulevard. Manitoba Corporation runs an industrial recycling facility on Geraldine Avenue. Precision Office Furniture Installation and Amerevent Tent Party Wedding & Event Rentals operate out of warehouse space on Union Boulevard, and Taylor Scientific wholesales lab and scientific supplies from Semple Avenue. The St. Louis Police Department’s North Patrol Division is headquartered on Union Boulevard inside the corridor. Imo’s Pizza on Natural Bridge Avenue is the one storefront most people passing through would actually recognize.
Anyone searching this corridor is far more likely to be a business owner, a job seeker, a supplier, or a driver passing through than someone looking for a place to shop or eat. Demand here runs on warehouse and distribution space, contracting and trade services, and fleet maintenance — the kinds of businesses that keep freight, buildings, and equipment moving along the I-70 corridor. It is a smaller, more specialized market than a retail district, and this guide reflects that honestly rather than dressing it up as something it isn’t.
Mark Twain I-70 Industrial’s business activity is built around heavy industry, logistics, and trade services along the I-70 freight corridor and the Natural Bridge / North Kingshighway / West Florissant arteries. The listings on this page are verified businesses physically located inside that boundary — industrial real estate, contracting, commercial recycling, fleet and equipment services, wholesale supply, and one longtime pizza shop — not businesses pulled in from elsewhere in the city to pad out the list.
Image: The Mark Twain / I-70 Industrial corridor — north St. Louis’s logistics-and-freight backbone along Interstate 70 and Natural Bridge Road

St. Louis runs hot, humid summers and cold winters here like anywhere else in the metro, but weather rarely slows the corridor down — warehousing, contracting, and freight keep moving through every season.

### Frequently Asked Questions 
Q. What defines the Mark Twain I-70 Industrial neighborhood? 
A. Mark Twain I-70 Industrial is a working freight-and-industrial corridor in north St. Louis, zip 63120, bounded by Interstate 70 to the north and Natural Bridge Road to the south, with North Kingshighway and West Florissant Avenue as its main east-west routes. It is anchored by the Union 70 Center industrial park and is a separate place from the residential Mark Twain neighborhood next door — same name, different function.

Q. How does St Louis Near Me Directory help Mark Twain I-70 Industrial businesses? 
A. St Louis Near Me Directory gives corridor businesses a schema-optimized listing built around search terms tied to Interstate 70, Natural Bridge Road, North Kingshighway, and Union 70 Center. Paid plans add Google Business Profile cleanup, review management, and ongoing content, helping the contractors, suppliers, and service providers along this corridor get found by the procurement managers, fleet operators, and residents searching for them.

Q. What types of businesses are most common in Mark Twain I-70 Industrial? 
A. The corridor runs on trade and logistics: general contracting, roofing, industrial recycling, office-furniture installation, commercial tire and fleet service, event-equipment rental, and lab-supply wholesaling cluster around Union Boulevard, Brown Avenue, and Semple Avenue near the Union 70 Center industrial park. Imo’s Pizza is the one consumer stop on the page; nearly everything else here sells to other businesses, not to walk-in shoppers.

Q. What kinds of dining, retail, and recreation options are available in Mark Twain I-70 Industrial? 
A. Very few. This is a working industrial corridor, not a shopping or dining district. Imo’s Pizza on Natural Bridge Avenue is the only sit-down or carryout option verified on this page. The rest of the corridor is contractors, a tire shop, a recycler, an event-rental company, and similar trade businesses with no retail storefronts, public seating, or recreation amenities to speak of.

Q. Are there neighborhood landmarks, parks, and historic sites in Mark Twain I-70 Industrial? 
A. The corridor’s defining landmark is the Union 70 Center industrial park itself, built into the interchange of Interstate 70 and Natural Bridge Road. The St. Louis Police Department’s North Patrol Division is headquartered on Union Boulevard inside the boundary. There are no traditional parks or historic tourist sites within these boundaries — the corridor’s identity is industrial and functional, not scenic.

Q. What is it like to live in Mark Twain I-70 Industrial? 
A. Almost nobody lives inside this corridor itself — it’s built for warehouses, contractors, and freight, not housing, which is different from the separate, residential Mark Twain neighborhood next door. On a given day the people here are mostly employees, drivers, and business owners working the corridor’s contracting, recycling, and logistics operations, plus officers working out of the North Patrol division on Union Boulevard.

Q. How do residents and visitors get around Mark Twain I-70 Industrial? 
A. By road. Interstate 70 forms the corridor’s north edge, Natural Bridge Road runs along the south, and North Kingshighway and West Florissant Avenue carry east-west traffic through it. The corridor is built for trucks, fleet vehicles, and commuting workers moving freight and materials in and out — not for foot traffic between destinations, since there is little to walk to.

Q. How can residents and visitors explore more services around Mark Twain I-70 Industrial? 
A. Start at StLouisMissouriNearMe.com’s neighborhood guides. St Louis Near Me Directory lists verified corridor businesses — from the Union 70 Center industrial park to contractors, a tire shop, an office-furniture installer, a wholesaler, and Imo’s Pizza — with ratings, addresses, and phone numbers, plus guides to the other 79 St. Louis neighborhoods for comparison.

### FAQ – St Louis Tile Contractors Map 

### Q. How much does it cost to fully tile a bathroom? 
A.  Fully tiling a bathroom typically runs about $1,500 to $8,000 or more, depending on the room's size, the tile you choose, and how much you cover — floor only versus floor, shower, and walls. Labor is the biggest driver. In the St. Louis area, compare a few tile contractors on this map and get itemized quotes before you commit.

### Q. How much do contractors charge per square foot for tile? 
A.  Tile contractors generally charge about $7 to $25 per square foot installed, with materials and labor quoted separately. The rate climbs with intricate patterns, small mosaic tile, and shower or wall work versus a plain floor. Because St. Louis rates vary by contractor and job, line up a few quotes from tile pros on this map to know your real number.

### Q. How much should labor cost for tile installation? 
A.  Labor is usually the largest share of a tile job, commonly $4 to $14 per square foot or a set day rate, and it rises with demolition of old tile, waterproofing, prep, and detailed layouts. In the St. Louis area, the honest way to gauge fair labor is itemized estimates — the map lets you compare several tile contractors quickly.

### Q. Is it worth tiling the whole bathroom? 
A.  For many St. Louis homeowners it is: tile resists moisture, lasts decades, and helps resale — though full floor-to-ceiling tile costs more than tiling just the wet areas. Whether it pays off comes down to your budget and how long you'll stay in the home. A local tile contractor from this map can walk you through the trade-offs.

### Q. Is it cheaper to tile a shower or use panels? 
A.  Shower wall panels are usually cheaper and faster to install than tile, while tile costs more upfront but lasts longer and offers far more design options. For St. Louis bathrooms, the right call depends on budget, style, and how long you plan to keep the home. Compare tile contractors on this map to price a tiled shower against panels.

### Q. Is a map pin enough to promote my tile business? 
A.  Map pins show where you work, but they carry only limited contact and basic details. A full listing on St Louis Near Me Directory gives your tile business room for a rich description, project photos, services, offers, and reviews — plus the local SEO and backlink value that helps St. Louis homeowners find and call you.

“Hey Google, find a plumber near me.” “Siri, who’s the best HVAC company in O’Fallon?” When a St. Louisan asks out loud — from their phone, car, or smart speaker — the assistant usually reads back one business. There’s no page two in voice. You’re the answer, or you’re invisible.
Voice search optimization positions your business to be that single, spoken answer when nearby customers ask.

### What Voice Search Optimization Involves
Tuned for how people actually talk to their devices:

### Conversational Content
Content written the natural, question-and-answer way people speak — not the way they type.

### FAQ & Q&A
Clear answers to the real questions customers ask, which voice assistants love to read back.

### Google Business Profile
A complete profile — the source voice assistants pull hours, location, and “near me” answers from.

### Reviews
Strong reviews that help assistants confidently name you as “the best” nearby option.

### Featured-Answer Targeting
Structuring content to win the snippet and direct answers that voice results read from.

### Mobile & Speed
A fast, mobile-friendly presence, since most voice searches happen on phones.

### Win the “Near Me” Moment, Hands-Free
Most voice searches are local and high-intent — someone driving, cooking, or on the move who needs a business now . The work overlaps with local SEO: a strong Google Business Profile, real reviews, fast mobile pages, and clear answers. Get those right and you win the typed search and the spoken one.

### FAQ – St Louis Window Companies Near You

### Q. What is the average cost of replacement windows?
A.  The national average is about $600 to $750 per window installed, with a typical range of $450 to $1,500 depending on material, size, and features. Vinyl is the most affordable at $650 to $1,300, while fiberglass runs $1,100 to $2,200. In St. Louis, older homes with non-standard openings often need custom sizes, which nudges the price up.

### Q. Is it worth replacing 20 year old windows?
A.  Usually yes. Twenty-year-old windows are near the end of their useful life, and if they’re drafty, hard to operate, or fogged between panes, new energy-efficient units cut heating and cooling bills and improve comfort — a real payoff in St. Louis’s hot summers and cold winters. Replacement also removes old single-pane glass and reduces outside noise.

### Q. What time of year are windows the cheapest?
A.  Late fall and winter are typically the cheapest time to buy replacement windows, because demand slows and installers offer off-season deals. Installation is still doable in St. Louis winters — crews replace one window at a time to limit heat loss. Spring and summer are the busiest and priciest, so booking in the off-season can save money and get you on the schedule faster.

### Q. Is it cheaper to replace all windows at once?
A.  Per window, yes. Doing the whole house at once spreads the crew’s setup and travel over more units and often unlocks volume pricing, so it usually costs less each than replacing a few at a time. A whole-house job of about 10 windows commonly runs $4,500 to $15,000. If the budget is tight, prioritize the worst-performing and street-facing windows first.

### Q. What is the average cost to replace 12 windows in a home?
A.  Replacing 12 windows in the St. Louis area typically runs about $5,400 to $18,000, based on roughly $450 to $1,500 per window installed. Vinyl keeps it toward the lower end; wood or fiberglass and custom sizes push it higher. Older homes with non-standard openings cost more because each window may need to be custom-made to fit.
