By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of West County — explore the whole region in our West County restaurant guide .
Creve Coeur runs along Olive Boulevard, one of the most internationally diverse restaurant stretches in all of St. Louis County. One drive turns up Syrian kebabs, two Korean BBQ houses, vegan Indian street food, a French patisserie that's been here since 1981, and Italian with real Hill pedigree. The chain apps see a strip mall; locals see a passport. (Heads-up: some of these show “St. Louis 63141” on Google but physically sit inside Creve Coeur.)
From a Syrian grill to a karaoke-and-bulgogi hybrid, here's where to eat in Creve Coeur.
It's all about Olive Boulevard (63141) — a single corridor with one of the metro's deepest benches of international food. A few spots close Sundays or Mondays, and lunch out here is a steal. Don't be thrown by “St. Louis” mailing addresses on a few of these; they're Creve Coeur.

### Layali Halab
Layali Halab is one of the only dedicated Syrian kitchens in the whole region — chef Mustafa Mustafa cooked professionally in Syria for a decade before opening this Aleppo-style spot. Charcoal kebabs, falafel, hummus, and a complimentary lentil soup for dine-in. Named for the “nights of Aleppo.”
📍 10477 Old Olive Street Rd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Bombay Food Junkies
Bombay Food Junkies is the area's only fully plant-based Indian spot — founded by Bombay natives Krupa and Sid, who ran St. Louis's first all-vegetarian Indian food truck back in 2013. Bombay-style chaats, a vegan “chicken” sandwich, samosas, and dairy-free shakes.
📍 12955 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Il Bel Lago
Il Bel Lago is brothers Frank and Carmelo Gabriele carrying their family's Hill pedigree out to Olive — they grew up at their father's landmark Giovanni's. The broiled veal chop with black truffle sauce is the dish that converts truffle skeptics. The dressy Italian.
📍 11631 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### La Bonne Bouchée Patisserie & Café
La Bonne Bouchée has been St. Louis's trusted French bakery since 1981 — a genuine Parisian-style patisserie with café classics like Croque Monsieur, Quiche Lorraine, and French onion soup. Pastry, coffee, and a long local history.
📍 12344 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Joo Joo Restaurant & Karaoke
Joo Joo is the Korean BBQ-and-karaoke hybrid — grill your own meat, then book a private karaoke room. Sauce Magazine has called its barbecue some of the finest in St. Louis; the kori gom tang oxtail soup is a standout. The fun night out.
📍 12937 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Seoul Garden
Seoul Garden is the family-owned all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ spot with a grill built into every table — cook your own bulgogi and spicy pork ribs, with bibimbap and soft tofu soup on the side. Hands-on and generous.
📍 10441 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Orzo Mediterranean Grill
Orzo is the Greek and Mediterranean fast-casual spot from Nick and Laura Cowlen — the duo behind the “Go Gyro Go!” food truck — tucked by the fountain in the City Space strip. Gyros, wraps, salads, and bowls. The great quick lunch.
📍 11627 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Timothy's
Timothy's is the “fine-casual” American spot punching above its strip-corridor address — a small seasonal menu with a lobster pot pie, steak frites, an exceptional wine program, and superb service at approachable prices. The neighborhood sleeper.
📍 12710 Olive Blvd, Creve Coeur, MO 63141

### Why this town matters
Creve Coeur's Olive Boulevard is a global food tour disguised as a suburban strip — Syrian, two kinds of Korean BBQ, vegan Indian, French pastry, Hill Italian, all in a few minutes' drive. The chain apps can't tell a decade-trained Aleppo chef from the franchise next door. We can.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in Creve Coeur, MO?
For a standout, locals point to the Korean BBQ — Joo Joo (Sauce calls its barbecue among the metro's finest) and Seoul Garden (all-you-can-eat). For dressier, Il Bel Lago brings real Hill Italian pedigree.
Why is Olive Boulevard known for food?
A single drive turns up Syrian (Layali Halab), Korean (Joo Joo, Seoul Garden), vegan Indian (Bombay Food Junkies), Greek (Orzo), French pastry (La Bonne Bouchée), and Italian (Il Bel Lago) — one of the most internationally diverse restaurant stretches in St. Louis County.
Where's a good quick lunch in Creve Coeur?
Orzo Mediterranean Grill (gyros and bowls), Bombay Food Junkies (chaats and vegan plates), and La Bonne Bouchée (quiche and French onion soup) — all fast, all genuinely local.
Are some Creve Coeur restaurants listed as “St. Louis”?
Yes — a few (Il Bel Lago, Joo Joo, Layali Halab) show a “St. Louis 63141” mailing address but physically sit on Olive inside Creve Coeur.

### Plan your Creve Coeur visit
A gyro lunch at Orzo, a French pastry at La Bonne Bouchée, then Korean BBQ and karaoke at Joo Joo. For more local spots across the metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Drive about half an hour south of St. Louis along the Mississippi and you hit Crystal City — a town that exists because of glass . They mined silica sand out of the ground here, built what was once the largest plate-glass plant on earth, and named the place for the crystal-clear product it made. The plant's gone now, but the town it built is still standing, still independent, and — turns out — still feeds you well.
Crystal City and neighboring Festus blur together so completely that locals just say "the Twin Cities," but Crystal City has its own two main drags — Truman Boulevard and Bailey Road — lined with the kind of spots that don't exist anywhere else: a 1948 burger stand that's cash-only on purpose, a bike shop that's also a wood-fired pizzeria, a Chinese place that's been family-run since 1982. Here's where to eat on the Crystal City side.
A couple of these keep old-school habits — Gordon's is cash only (there's an ATM inside), and a few of the diners close Mondays. Worth a heads-up before you go. And here's the move locals know: pair your meal with the Crystal City Underground , the 400-foot-deep flooded silica mine beneath the old glassworks. It runs boat tours, sand volleyball, and the only underground disc golf course on the planet. Eat above ground, play below it.

### Gordon's Stoplight Drive-In
Start at the landmark. Gordon's Stoplight Drive-In has been griddling "the best hamburgers in the world" since 1948 — same corner, same simple idea, cash only, and a line that proves the formula still works after 75-plus years. This is a genuine piece of Jefferson County, served on a tray.
📍 500 Bailey Rd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Pedal'N Pi
Only in a town like this: Pedal'N Pi is a bike shop and a wood-fired Neapolitan pizzeria under one roof. Owner Chris Creed opened it in 2021, and the crust earns the raves — including from gluten-free eaters, who swear it's the best GF pizza they've had anywhere. Fix a flat, eat a pie, leave grinning.
📍 514 Bailey Rd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Kettelhut's Smokehouse
For smoke, Kettelhut's is the family-owned Memphis-style smokehouse on Truman Boulevard, putting out brisket and pulled pork that regulars describe as melt-in-your-mouth — and a sleeper burger that surprises everyone who orders it. Everything's smoked fresh on-site daily, the way BBQ is supposed to be.
📍 1267 N Truman Blvd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Lam's Garden
Some places earn their spot just by lasting. Lam's Garden has served family-style Chinese here since 1982 — four-plus decades of one family feeding the same town. In an era when restaurants flicker out in eighteen months, that kind of staying power is its own recommendation.
📍 510 Bailey Rd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Thai Rama
When you want something cooked precisely to order, Thai Rama does from-scratch Thai on Truman Boulevard, every dish built with fresh produce and dialed to your heat tolerance — all the way up to "Thai hot" if you're feeling brave. It's the kind of careful, independent cooking a small town is lucky to have.
📍 606 N Truman Blvd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Main Street Cafe
For the home-style breakfast-and-lunch routine, Main Street Cafe on Truman is the early-morning diner locals have leaned on for years — fried chicken, BBQ, seafood, and a 6 a.m. open Tuesday through Saturday. Closed Mondays; otherwise, it's the town's reliable plate.
📍 902 N Truman Blvd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Iguanas Mexican Grill
Iguanas brings the street tacos, fajitas, enchiladas, and seafood, plus late hours for when the night runs long — an authentic family Mexican spot that opened in 2021 and quickly became a Truman Boulevard regular.
📍 907 N Truman Blvd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### P'sghetti's Pasta & Sandwiches
If you want something unmistakably St. Louis, P'sghetti's does Provel-laden Italian subs, homemade sweet bread, and big plates of pasta — a locally owned, St. Louis-family operation that opened its Crystal City spot in the old frozen-custard building. Toasted ravioli energy in the best way.
📍 101 S Truman Blvd, Crystal City, MO 63019

### Why this little town matters
Crystal City was built as a company town for the glassworks, a place that literally manufactured something you could see through. The plant closed in 1990, but the town didn't — and the proof is on Truman and Bailey, where a 1948 drive-in, a bike-shop pizzeria, a 1982 family Chinese restaurant, and a daily smokehouse all hold their corners. That's a kind of resilience the chain-logo maps off the highway will never show you.
That's the whole reason we built a hyper-local directory. Search St Louis Near Me Directory for Crystal City and Jefferson County before you go — and if you're working your way through the county, our De Soto guide and Hillsboro guide are close by.
And if you run a Crystal City spot — a taco truck, a bakery, a weekend pop-up — a listing is how the next carful of explorers finds you on the way to the Underground.

### FAQ
What's the most famous place to eat in Crystal City?
Gordon's Stoplight Drive-In — griddling hamburgers since 1948, cash only, and still drawing a line. It's a genuine local landmark.
Is the food in Crystal City actually in Crystal City, or Festus?
The twin cities blur together, but everything in this guide is confirmed in Crystal City proper (ZIP 63019) — on Truman Boulevard and Bailey Road — not over the line in Festus.
What's the unique thing to do in Crystal City besides eat?
Visit the Crystal City Underground — a 400-foot-deep flooded silica-sand mine left from the glass industry, now offering boat tours, sand volleyball, and the world's only underground disc golf course.
Are there independent restaurants in Crystal City, or mostly chains?
Plenty of independents — a 1948 drive-in, a wood-fired bike-shop pizzeria, a 1982 family Chinese spot, a daily smokehouse, two Mexican options, and more. The chains exist, but the local spots are the reason to stop.

### Plan your Crystal City day
Grab a cash-only burger at Gordon's, a wood-fired pie at Pedal'N Pi, and a boat tour of the Underground. For more local spots across Jefferson County and the St. Louis metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Dardenne Prairie is small, and its whole independent food scene basically fits in one walkable plaza — the Town Square / Harmony Meadows development on Highway N, anchored by the Schnucks Town Square grocery. That's actually the charm: you can park once and hit a sports-bar-and-grill, a cult-favorite Indian street-food counter, a Thai kitchen, a Chinese takeout, and a brand-new dessert shop without moving your car. The 63368 ZIP blurs into O'Fallon and Lake St. Louis, so we kept to the genuine Dardenne Prairie spots.
From a "mess hall" Indian counter to deep-fried dough balls next to the pub, here's where to eat in Dardenne Prairie.
It's essentially one cluster — the Town Square / Harmony Meadows development on Hwy N (63368). Because the 63368 ZIP is shared with O'Fallon and Lake St. Louis, many "Dardenne Prairie" listings online (Tully's Taproom, Thai Gourmet) are actually O'Fallon. For more variety, O'Fallon and Lake St. Louis are minutes away.

### Town Square Pub N Grub
The town anchor — and its #1-rated spot. Town Square Pub N Grub is the locally owned sports bar and grill that doubles as the town's living room — full bar, arcade games, wall of TVs, live music. Smash burgers, loaded nachos, fish tacos. In 2025 the owners opened the Sugar Shack right next door.
📍 7843 Town Square Ave, Dardenne Prairie, MO 63368

### Desi Vilas
The hidden gem locals call "the mess hall." Desi Vilas is the woman-led South Indian street-food counter with a cult daily-deal following — Tuesday chaat, Wednesday biryani, Thursday dosas — and famous Mysore bondas (crispy, spicy potato fritters) and punugulu. Built on a passion for authentic Indian at fair prices.
📍 324 Harmony Meadows Court, Dardenne Prairie, MO 63368

### Thai 4 U
Thai 4 U is the single-location independent Thai kitchen — pad Thai, curries, stir-fries, soups, traditional recipes dialed to St. Charles County tastes. Casual, family-friendly, open daily.
📍 318 Harmony Meadows Court, Dardenne Prairie, MO 63368

### Happy China
Happy China is the Town Square strip's reliable Chinese takeout standby — chef's specialties, sweet & sour, lo mein, Mei Fun, and a notable vegetarian section. Closed Mondays, late on weekends.
📍 7871 Town Square Ave, Dardenne Prairie, MO 63368

### Town Square Sugar Shack
Town Square Sugar Shack is the brand-new (summer 2025) sweet sibling to the Pub N Grub, right next door — deep-fried dough balls dusted in cinnamon sugar and smothered in caramel and chocolate. Built for families after a burger.
📍 7843 Town Square Ave, Dardenne Prairie, MO 63368

### Why this town matters
Dardenne Prairie's whole local food scene fits in one walkable plaza on Highway N — a pub, a cult Indian counter, a Thai kitchen, a Chinese takeout, and a dessert shop, all steps apart. The apps blur it with O'Fallon; we map the genuine Town Square cluster and point you next door for more.

### FAQ
What's the best place to eat in Dardenne Prairie, MO?
The standout is Desi Vilas — a woman-led South Indian street-food counter locals call "the mess hall" for its rotating daily specials and famous Mysore bondas. Town Square Pub N Grub is the #1-rated town anchor.
Is Dardenne Prairie's food scene all in one place?
Pretty much — the independents concentrate in the Town Square / Harmony Meadows development on Hwy N (anchored by Schnucks Town Square), so you can hit a pub, Indian, Thai, Chinese, and dessert without moving your car.
Are some "Dardenne Prairie" restaurants actually in O'Fallon?
Yes — the 63368 ZIP is shared with O'Fallon and Lake St. Louis, so spots like Tully's Taproom and Thai Gourmet show up under Dardenne Prairie but are actually O'Fallon. Stick to the Town Square cluster for the true list.
Where's more food near Dardenne Prairie?
O'Fallon and Lake St. Louis are minutes away with much deeper benches — see our O'Fallon MO and Lake St. Louis guides.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Have you ever found yourself driving through a small town and wondering where the locals actually eat — not the highway chain with the glowing sign, but the place with six trucks parked out front at noon and a regular's name half-remembered by the woman behind the counter?
In De Soto, that place isn't hard to find. Tucked into southwest Jefferson County along Joachim Creek, this old railroad town has quietly held onto something a lot of suburbs traded away years ago: a real, walkable Main Street where almost every kitchen is somebody's livelihood, not a corporate franchise. Whether you grew up here, you're passing through on the way to the lake, or you just like hunting down the genuine article, here's where to eat in De Soto.

### Junction Cafe
Start where De Soto starts its mornings. Junction Cafe opens early — 6 a.m. on weekdays — and trades in exactly what a railroad-town diner should: all-day breakfast, hearty "Junction" sandwiches, and an open-face roast beef that arrives under a quilt of gravy. It's the kind of counter where the coffee never quite runs dry.
📍 106 S Main St, De Soto, MO 63020

### El Lobo Rojo
Right across the Main Street divide, chef Jose Maria Lopez cooks the Jalisco-style Mexican food he grew up on at El Lobo Rojo — tacos, burritos, fajitas, chimichangas, the works. It's independent, it's got its own loyal following, and the portions don't apologize for themselves.
📍 106 N Main St, De Soto, MO 63020

### Sherwood's Classic Eats
A De Soto success story in motion: Sherwood's has been feeding the area since 2018 and moved onto Main Street at the end of 2024, bringing along its handmade pizzas, pasta, and a stacked signature sandwich called "The John Wayne." Subs, salads, wraps — it's the dependable, made-to-order kind of spot every town needs and not every town has.
📍 122 N Main St, De Soto, MO 63020

### Cafe Smok N Pi
Just outside downtown on Route 21, Cafe Smok N Pi does the thing St. Louis-area smokehouses do best — and the move here is the pork steak , that gloriously regional cut you won't find done right just anywhere. Brick-oven pizza rounds out the menu, and live music takes over Friday and Saturday nights from 6 to 9.
📍 12636 State Route 21, De Soto, MO 63020

### Pogolino's
When De Soto wants pizza, a lot of De Soto goes to Pogolino's — the local Italian-leaning pizzeria and Chamber of Commerce mainstay that opens daily at 11. Nothing flashy, just the neighborhood pizza joint doing what it's done for years.
📍 530 N 2nd St, De Soto, MO 63020

### Just Be Kind Café
For a slower morning, Just Be Kind Café is the exposed-brick, plant-filled coffee shop and bakery the town didn't used to have. Specialty coffee, house-baked goods, and custom cakes, open weekday mornings into the afternoon. The name pretty much tells you the vibe.
📍 426 S Main St, De Soto, MO 63020

### LaChance Vineyards
And when you want to make an evening of it, LaChance Vineyards is the destination — an 80-acre family farm winery in De Soto's rolling hills, founded in 2010 by Harold and Tami Hamby and named for Harold's French great-grandfather. Roughly 8,000 vines, a farm-to-table menu, and live music; it's been named the St. Louis area's #1 winery more than once by the local food press.
📍 12237 Peter Moore Ln, De Soto, MO 63020

### A town with more going on than you'd guess
De Soto wears its history on its sleeve — the Iron Mountain railroad rolled in back in 1858 and made this a genuine "train town," and the place still sits along Joachim Creek , where the locals race rubber ducks every fall. (Trivia for your table: in 1980, De Soto was the U.S. town closest to the mean center of the entire country's population.) The De Soto Fall Festival each September turns N Main Street into a street fair, food vendors and all.
It's a lot of character for one small Jefferson County town — and a perfect example of why a hyper-local directory beats a generic national app. Search St Louis Near Me Directory for De Soto and you'll turn up the businesses the big platforms never bother to list. The Main Street core is overwhelmingly independent — diners, a Mexican spot, pizza, a coffee bakery, a smokehouse, and a destination winery, all locally owned. That's the reason to get off the highway.

Junction Cafe is the early-riser favorite, open at 6 a.m. weekdays with all-day breakfast and big diner plates.

Each September on N Main Street — arts and crafts, a car show, a 5K, food vendors, and the famous Joachim Creek duck race. Check the current year's date before you go.

The landmark. London's Wing House has been frying since 1963 — one of the oldest Black-owned wing joints in St. Louis, founded by Dale and Hildred London and now run by their son Patrick. Cathy's Kitchen To-Go is the Dellwood carryout sibling of the famous Ferguson restaurant — Cajun chicken pasta, blackened shrimp alfredo, crispy catfish — built on 30 years of family recipes owner Cathy collected traveling the country. 📍 10198 W Florissant Ave, Dellwood, MO 63136

Hunan Chop Suey is the Dellwood Village strip's go-to fast Chinese counter — chop suey, fried rice, wings, St. Louis-style — and it's right in the City of Dellwood's own business directory. The dependable neighborhood takeout.

### Village Bar
Village Bar is the corridor's living history — the building started as an 1872 post office and feed store and has poured beer since just after Prohibition, arguably the oldest watering hole on Manchester. Get the "Better Burger" (fresh, never-frozen) and the award-winning hand-breaded onion rings. Open till 1 a.m.
📍 12247 Manchester Rd, Des Peres, MO 63131

### Surf & Sirloin
Surf & Sirloin is the family-owned old-school steakhouse Larry Karagiannis opened in 1994 — filet mignon with classic Béarnaise, seared Maine scallops, fish bought whole and inspected on-site. The brickwork-and-high-ceilings room where West County couples have celebrated anniversaries for 30 years.
📍 13090 Manchester Rd, Des Peres, MO 63131

### Three Kings Public House
Three Kings is the gastropub whose breaded chicken wings earned national attention — plus award-winning burgers and a deep craft-beer list, ingredients from Missouri and Illinois farmers. It's a small St. Louis-grown group (four locations), and this is the Des Peres one.
📍 11925 Manchester Rd, Des Peres, MO 63131

### Rosalita's Cantina
Rosalita's is the big-blue-marble-bar Tex-Mex and tequila spot — tableside guacamole, Cadillac Fajitas, and a house margarita locals routinely call the best in town, under starry light fixtures with a patio.

### Casa de Tres Reyes
Casa de Tres Reyes is the colorful, genuinely kid-friendly independent Mexican spot doing birria tacos, cheese-crusted burritos, and empanadas — one of the few places doing Mexican breakfast plus birria and margaritas under one roof.
📍 1181 Colonnade Center, Des Peres, MO 63131

### Tiger Soup Dumplings
Tiger Soup Dumplings is the brand's second, larger location — steamed or pan-fried soup dumplings (pork, chicken, beef, shrimp, even cheese), rice rolls, and fruit tea, all handmade in a sleek modern space.
📍 13311 Manchester Rd, Des Peres, MO 63131

### Tiger 88 Banh Mi & Boba
Tiger 88 is the bright Vietnamese counter café (a separate business from the soup dumpling spot despite the shared "Tiger") — smoky grilled-pork banh mi with nuoc cham, pho, and a wide boba list.
📍 12055 Manchester Rd, Des Peres, MO 63131

### Flavors Indian Cuisine
Flavors is the unflashy neighborhood Indian room West County regulars rely on — tandoori chicken, lamb korma, biryani, and a rotating lunch special, in a simple, sophisticated dining hall.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Dupo is a small rail town in the American Bottom flatlands south of East St. Louis — its odd little name a worn-down version of Prairie du Pont ("bridge prairie"), from the French colonists who settled here around 1750 and built one of Illinois's first wagon-road bridges. It grew up around the Missouri Pacific switching yards, and it still feels like a railroad town. Here's the pleasant surprise: for a village of about 4,000, Dupo punches well above its weight on food — a women-owned scratch café, a lakeside tavern with live music, an independent Mexican spot the town adores.
When you're down by the bluffs and hungry, here's where to eat in Dupo.
Most spots sit along Main Street and the side streets just off it, with a couple out toward the lakes. The café is a morning operation; the taverns run late. A few are newer, so a quick hours check helps. Dupo sits about ten miles from Cahokia Mounds — the UNESCO World Heritage site — so it's an easy pairing with a visit there.

### Sugar & Sage Cafe
Start at the town's new darling. Sugar & Sage is a family- and women-owned scratch café — locally roasted coffee, made-from-scratch breakfast and lunch, and homemade baked goods, with a kids' play area. It got a St. Louis TV feature, sources from local small businesses, and has quickly become the heart of Dupo's mornings.
📍 115 N 2nd St, Dupo, IL 62239

### Triple Lakes Tavern
The destination spot. Triple Lakes Tavern sits out by the lakes with a patio and live music — smoked cheeseburgers, chicken dumplings, "Fried Chicken Sundays," and a Friday fish-and-wings spread. The lean-back, stay-a-while pick.
📍 8055 Triple Lakes Rd, Dupo, IL 62239

### The Mexican
The Mexican on South Main is the independent Mexican spot the town genuinely loves — reviewers rave about the garlic shrimp fajitas, the margaritas, and a signature white dip with the chips. One regular called it "such an amazing addition to our little town," which is exactly the vibe.
📍 200 S Main St, Dupo, IL 62239

### Dairy Land
Dairy Land (you'll also see it as Dawn's Dairyland) is the classic small-town walk-up — burgers, hot wings, cheese sticks, corn dogs, fried cauliflower, malts, and soft-serve. The owner-run treat-and-a-burger window every rail town should have.
📍 501 S Main St, Dupo, IL 62239

### 5th Street Billiards Bar & Grill
5th Street Billiards is the pool-hall-and-grill — burgers, wings, Italian beef, "coldest beer in town," and year-round pool leagues. The casual hang for a game and a plate.
📍 200 N 5th St, Dupo, IL 62239

### Judy's Corner
Judy's Corner is the spotless little neighborhood bar where owner Judy runs the room and the kitchen turns out pizza — a genuine local corner spot with a loyal following.
📍 534 S Main St, Dupo, IL 62239

### Why this little town matters
Dupo is a 270-year-old French-rooted rail town that the apps reduce to a couple of listings and a gas station — but it quietly fields a women-owned scratch café, a lakeside tavern with live music, a beloved independent Mexican spot, and a classic ice-cream-and-burger stand. For a village of 4,000 in the floodplain, that's a real food scene, and it's exactly the kind of overlooked local gem a hyper-local directory exists to surface.

Is there good food in Dupo, IL?
More than you'd expect for a town of 4,000 — Sugar & Sage Cafe (women-owned scratch café), Triple Lakes Tavern (lakeside, live music), The Mexican (a local favorite), and Dairy Land (a classic walk-up), plus a couple of neighborhood bar-and-grills.

Sugar & Sage Cafe on North 2nd Street — locally roasted coffee, scratch breakfast and baked goods, and a kids' play area.

Cahokia Mounds — the UNESCO World Heritage site and the largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico — is about ten miles away, an easy pairing with a meal in Dupo.
How did Dupo get its name?
It's a worn-down version of "Prairie du Pont" (French for "bridge prairie"), from the French colonists who settled here around 1750 and built one of Illinois's first wagon-road bridges. The railroad later shortened it to Dupo.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
East St. Louis has a real but thin food scene, and what survives is deeply local: old-school BBQ and soul food, defined less by ribs than by snoots — crispy fried pig snouts, a Metro East tradition. Two long-running pit institutions still serve them, alongside a late-night fish-and-chicken counter and the riverfront casino dining. People here get hungry too, and these are the genuinely local spots worth knowing — plus where to go nearby for more.
From a drive-through line wrapped around the building to cash-only ribs since the '70s, here's where to eat in East St. Louis.
This is a thin market with a lot of mislabeled listings — many “East St. Louis” results are actually in Washington Park, Cahokia Heights, or across the river. We kept to verified East St. Louis ZIPs (62201/62203/62205/62207). Hours are limited and a couple of spots are cash-only — a same-day check helps. For a fuller sit-down meal, Belleville and Fairview Heights are a short drive southeast.

### Big Mama's BBQ Express
Big Mama's has been smoking since 2001 — crispy snoots, meaty rib tips, and the over-the-top “Cooter Comeback Sammich” (double patties or pulled meat, “cooter sauce,” loaded with fries), plus house-made cakes. The drive-through line famously wraps around the building; locals plan around the wait.
📍 5900 St. Clair Ave, East St. Louis, IL 62203

### Sandy's Bar B Q
Sandy's is the old-school BBQ shack in business since the 1970s — crispy snoots with perfect texture and juicy, tender ribs under homemade sauce. It's cash only, no cards, no call-aheads: you show up, you order at the counter. A genuine decades-old neighborhood institution. (Use the 327 S 15th St location; verify the limited hours.)
📍 327 S 15th St, East St. Louis, IL 62207

### Pop's Fish & Chicken
Pop's is the casual local fish-and-chicken counter — fried catfish-nugget dinners, ten-wing dinners, plus burgers, Philly steak, and gyros — and it's open late, until about 11:30 p.m. most nights, one of the few genuinely late-night bites in the city.
📍 2413 State St, East St. Louis, IL 62205

### Bridgeway & That Chickn' Place (at the Casino)
The riverfront option. Bridgeway (New American sit-down) and That Chickn' Place (wings and chicken) operate inside the downtown casino at 200 Front St — casino-run, not locally owned, but the only riverfront dining in the city, with downtown St. Louis skyline views and a kitchen open into the early-morning hours.
📍 200 Front St, East St. Louis, IL 62201

### Why this town matters
East St. Louis is a thin, high-turnover market — which is exactly why the surviving local pits matter. A 50-year cash-only BBQ shack and a snoot-famous drive-through are the real story here, and the chain apps are a minefield of closed and mislabeled spots. ### FAQ
What's the signature food in East St. Louis, IL?
Snoots — crispy fried pig snouts — are the regional BBQ tradition, and both surviving pit institutions (Big Mama's and Sandy's) are known for them. It's the dish that defines local BBQ here more than ribs.
What's the most old-school spot in East St. Louis?
Sandy's Bar B Q — in business since the 1970s, cash-only and in-person-only. A 50-year neighborhood holdout in a city that's lost most of its sit-down restaurants.
Is East St. Louis's food scene big?
Honestly, no — it's a thin market with high turnover and lots of mislabeled listings. A handful of genuine local BBQ and soul-food spots, plus the riverfront casino dining. For a fuller meal, Belleville and Fairview Heights are a short drive southeast.
Are some “East St. Louis” restaurants actually in other towns?
Yes — in 2021 Centreville, Cahokia, and Alorton merged into Cahokia Heights, and many southern-edge listings fall there or in Washington Park (62204). Real East St. Louis ZIPs are 62201, 62203, 62205, 62206, and 62207.

Edwardsville is the Madison County seat and a genuine college town — home to SIUE, a historic Main Street, a Route 66 alignment, and the 1890 Leclaire model-village district. All of that adds up to one of the strongest independent food scenes in the Metro East: chef-driven New American, hand-pulled pasta, scratch bakeries, and a cocktail-and-brunch culture that punches well above a town of 27,000.
From a Beard-pedigree kitchen to the town's oldest bar, here's where to eat in Edwardsville.
The independents split between historic downtown (Main Street, Vandalia, St. Louis Street) and the newer Plum Street / Route 157 corridor — both in 62025. A few are dinner-only or brunch-focused, so check first. Time a June trip for the Edwardsville Route 66 Festival (the 2026 edition coincides with Route 66's 100th birthday).

### Cleveland-Heath
Start at the flagship. Cleveland-Heath is downtown's chef-driven New American room — gourmet comfort food that earned its founding chef James Beard "Best Chef" semifinalist nods. A genuine destination, and the anchor of Edwardsville dining.
📍 106 N Main St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Mio Osteria
Mio Osteria is the family-owned Italian spot from Micah and Aerika Hopkin — casual lunch, upscale dinner, and a thoughtful cocktail-and-wine program, with a real owner-history pedigree in St. Louis kitchens. The grown-up Italian night.
📍 224 S Kansas St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Brick + Bramble
Brick + Bramble is the craft-cocktail bar and shareable-plates spot with a popular weekend brunch — a community staple on Plum Street. The place for a good drink and small plates.
📍 2323 Plum St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Café Birdie
Café Birdie is the breakfast-and-brunch café opened in 2023 by Edwardsville native Jenny Levi, who came home after 20-plus years cooking on the West Coast — a great local-roots story and a bright daily breakfast.
📍 120 S Main St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Sacred Grounds Cafe
Sacred Grounds is the downtown independent coffeehouse — organic breakfast and lunch, walls full of local art, a longtime community hangout. The morning anchor.
📍 233 N Main St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### 222 Artisan Bakery & Cafe
222 Artisan Bakery (on St. Louis Street, not Main) is the family-owned scratch bakery — fresh bread, cinnamon rolls, pastries, breakfast and sandwiches, plus sourdough pizzas on weekends. Run by a mom-and-son team.
📍 222 St. Louis St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Chava's Mexican Restaurant
Chava's is the family-owned authentic Mexican spot — recipes from Guadalajara, run by the Ybarra family since 2013. The dependable, made-fresh Mexican pick.
📍 217 E Vandalia St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Stagger Inn Again
Stagger Inn Again is Edwardsville's oldest continuously operating watering hole — a restaurant by day, a bar with live music by night. The historic local hang.
📍 104 E Vandalia St, Edwardsville, IL 62025

### Peel Wood Fired Pizza
Peel is the neo-Neapolitan wood-fired pizzeria that started right here in Edwardsville in 2008 (founded by two ex-pastry chefs) before growing into a small regional name. It's a local-born chain rather than a one-off, but the Edwardsville original is the real deal.
📍 100 Quartz Knoll, Edwardsville, IL 62025

Ellisville sits in far West County where Manchester Road runs past Clarkson, and its food packs into about a mile of that corridor — a stretch with serious staying power. A St. Louis pizza institution from 1968, a 30-year Chinese-Thai-Vietnamese spot, a golf-themed wing joint since 1993, plus newer stars like a Mexico City small-plates room and a Filipino mochi-donut shop. The trick out here is the city line: Manchester straddles Ellisville, Ballwin, and Winchester, so plenty of "Ellisville" listings aren't.
From a 1968 Provel-and-cracker-crust pizza to Mexico City small plates, here's where to eat in Ellisville.
Nearly every independent worth visiting sits along a one-mile stretch of Manchester Rd (roughly 15300–16100, 63011), with Mulligan's just off it on Clarkson. Watch the city line — a 63011 ZIP doesn't guarantee Ellisville (some nearby spots are Ballwin or Wildwood). Several are decades-old family institutions; a couple close Sundays or Mondays.

### Malinche Mexican Culinary Experience
The critics' darling. Malinche isn't your average taco shop — it's small plates inspired by the culinary traditions of Mexico City, in an intimate, elevated room that earned Feast Magazine and KSDK coverage. Order several plates and the chips-and-salsa with its local cult following.
📍 15939 Manchester Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

### Faraci Pizza
Faraci is a genuine 1968-vintage St. Louis pizza institution — thin, square-cut, cracker-crust, Provel-topped — still run by the family, with specialty pies like buffalo chicken and Mediterranean. The real St. Louis article. Closed Sundays.
📍 15430 Manchester Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

### Mulligan's Grill
Mulligan's has been the family-owned, golf-themed bar and grill since 1993 — menu items named after golf terms, and locals insist the only way to order the wings is "trashed" (extra-crispy). The neighborhood hang on Clarkson.
📍 11 Clarkson Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

### Golden Wok
Golden Wok is the 30-plus-year fixture that quietly grew from a Chinese carryout into a three-cuisine spot — Chinese, Thai, and Vietnamese under one roof. The dependable pan-Asian standby. Closed Sundays.
📍 15941 Manchester Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

### Tatva Cafe
Tatva is the vegetarian South Indian room where the dosas — crispy fermented rice-and-lentil crepes — are the draw, alongside South Indian curries and breakfast. A genuinely different option on the corridor.
📍 15801 Manchester Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

### Mochi Donut Factory
Mochi Donut Factory is the Filipino-family shop from high-school sweethearts Carlo and Jaen Henson (born and raised in Manila) who brought the chewy mochi donut to West County — churro, Fruity Pebbles, pineapple-passionfruit. Morning-and-early-afternoon only.
📍 16023 Manchester Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

### Fallon's Grill and Tap
Fallon's is the family-run Irish bar and grill — authentic pub fare (burgers, sandwiches, plus steak and seafood) and a whiskey bar, in a room that aims family-friendly. Closed Mondays.
📍 15850 Manchester Rd, Ellisville, MO 63011

Elsberry is a small far-north Lincoln County town of about 1,800 on Highway 79 — the Great River Road along the Mississippi — and for its size, the food scene is genuinely healthy: a real cluster of locally owned independents on North Main and Broadway. Every spot below appears on the City of Elsberry's own business-license list, the strongest "still open" signal there is. People here, and travelers on the river road, get hungry too — these are the real local favorites, no padding needed.
From a 6 a.m. biscuits-and-gravy diner to a deli-ice-cream-florist all under one roof, here's where to eat in Elsberry.
Most of the independents sit within a few walkable blocks on North Main Street and Broadway (63343), so a meal pairs naturally with a Great River Road / bald-eagle-watching trip. Several keep small-town hours — a couple are Thu–Sun only or daytime only — so call ahead. The only chain in town is a gas-station Hunt Brothers Pizza.

### The Pickle Barrel
The town's most-loved spot and the best hook anywhere — a wonderfully odd hybrid that's a deli counter, a hand-scooped ice-cream shop, AND a full florist/gift shop under one historic Broadway roof, with pinball and arcade machines. The chicken-bacon-ranch wrap, ice cream, and apple pie are the orders. Daytime only.
📍 401 Broadway St, Elsberry, MO 63343

### AJ's Tex-Mex & BBQ
The other point of local pride — a Tex-Mex-and-barbecue fusion named Elsberry Chamber Small Business of the Year two years running. Smoked BBQ plates alongside Tex-Mex, open late Thu–Sat (to ~1 a.m.) so it doubles as the evening hangout.
📍 451 N Main St, Elsberry, MO 63343

### Dos Primos
The family-run Mexican room — fajitas (chicken, steak, shrimp, Hawaiian), carne asada, and a white queso reviewers call "to die for." Open daily 11–9, the most consistent full-week hours in town. (One reviewer flat-out called it the best taco they've ever had.)
📍 457 N Main St, Elsberry, MO 63343

### Rachel's Restaurant
The home-cooking diner — open at 6 a.m. for biscuits and gravy and breakfast-for-lunch plates, where reviewers say they're treated "like family." The classic everybody-knows-everybody Main Street morning room (weekend hours shorten).
📍 447 N Main St, Elsberry, MO 63343

### Cadillac Bills
The burger joint — big smashed double cheeseburgers, chili cheese fries, a pork tenderloin sandwich, and fried catfish, with both dine-in and a drive-through (rare for a town this size). Closed Mondays.
📍 403 N Main St, Elsberry, MO 63343

### Shooters Saloon
The town's social hub on Broadway — boneless and "naked" wings, a French dip, and a Friday/weekend ribeye Steak Night, with a pool table, darts, and Wednesday poker. Kid-friendly until 9, then the late-night tavern.
📍 213 Broadway St, Elsberry, MO 63343

### Why this town matters
Elsberry punches way above its size — five strong sit-down independents plus a saloon, a local coffee shop (Southern Grace), and a BBQ trailer (Low N Slow), almost all on a couple of walkable blocks. For a far-north river town nobody writes about, that's a real food map, and it's the perfect lunch stop on a Highway 79 drive. We map it honestly.

### Sarah's on Central
Start downtown. Sarah's on Central is the café-and-cake shop doing breakfast, lunch, scratch desserts, specialty coffee, and cocktails — the brunch-and-dessert anchor of Central Avenue (the local outpost of the beloved Sarah's Cake Shop family). Closed Monday–Tuesday.
📍 127 S Central Ave, Eureka, MO 63025

### La Finca Coffee
La Finca brought authentic Colombian-style coffee to Eureka — fresh-roasted coffee, empanadas, breakfast burritos, the "La Finca Frappe," and vinyl Latin music. A genuinely distinctive independent and a local favorite.

### Chick-N-Elly's
Chick-N-Elly's is the beloved local breakfast spot and dive bar — all-day weekend breakfast, omelettes, and wings, with the kind of well-worn character a chain can't manufacture. A genuine Eureka institution.

### O'Dell's Irish Pub & Ale House
O'Dell's is the downtown Irish pub doing homemade Irish-American comfort — corned beef, bangers and mash, a Frisco melt, a bourbon pork chop — with a warm, authentic room and a big local following.

### Poor Richard's Restaurant & Sports Club
A family-owned bar and grill since 1982 , Poor Richard's is the wings-and-steaks game-day spot — decades of Eureka loyalty behind it. Just off the Central strip near Hwy 109.

### Joe Boccardi's Ristorante
Here's the heritage pick: Joe Boccardi's original location opened in Eureka in 1971 — hand-rolled St. Louis-style pizza, toasted ravioli, and pasta from the Boccardi family. It's since grown into a small regional family group, but this is the one that started it all.
📍 128 Boccardi Ln, Eureka, MO 63025

### Exit 11 Coffee Company
For the drive-thru fix, Exit 11 Coffee is the locally owned, award-winning roaster — small-batch beans and house-made organic syrups, "fast, fresh, organic, homemade." Eureka is its flagship, a homegrown St. Louis-region coffee name.
📍 527 N Central Ave, Eureka, MO 63025

Ferguson is one of St. Louis's original railroad suburbs — it started in 1855 when William Ferguson traded ten acres to the Wabash Railroad for a depot and the naming rights, making it the first rail stop connected straight to the city. That depot-town downtown still runs along South Florissant Road , the heart of the Ferguson CityWalk, and on a Saturday morning it fills up around one of the most beloved farmers markets in the region.
It's a tight-knit, proud little downtown, and the independent food here is genuinely good. Here's where to eat in Ferguson.
The walkable core is South Florissant Road downtown — most spots below are within a few blocks. The famous Ferguson Farmers Market runs Saturday mornings (8–noon, May–October) at Plaza at 501, moving indoors monthly in winter — a destination in itself. ### Cathy's Kitchen Restaurant & Diner
Start at the flagship. Cathy's Kitchen is the downtown diner owner Cathy Jenkins built from the recipes she gathered on a cross-country road trip — American comfort food with Cajun-Southern leanings, from shrimp and grits to Cajun chicken pasta to catfish. It's become the symbol of this downtown's heart and resilience, and the food more than earns the visit.
📍 250 S Florissant Rd, Ferguson, MO 63135

### King of Soul Cafe
King of Soul Cafe does exactly what the name promises — genuine soul food, locally owned, a few blocks down South Florissant. The kind of from-the-heart cooking that anchors a neighborhood.

### Good News Brewing – Ferguson
In 2026, Good News Brewing took over the longtime Ferguson Brewing space on South Florissant — craft beer and wood-fired pizza, family-friendly, run by longtime Ferguson residents. A new chapter for the downtown's craft-beer corner. (It's a fresh opening, so confirm current hours.)
📍 418 S Florissant Rd, Ferguson, MO 63135

### The Ferguson Farmers Market
Not a restaurant, but the heart of eating in Ferguson: the Ferguson Farmers Market runs Saturday mornings May through October at Plaza at 501 — produce, prepared food, baked goods, and live music, with a monthly indoor Winter Market the rest of the year. It's consistently ranked among the best markets in the metro and is reason enough to plan a Saturday here.
📍 501 S Florissant Rd, Ferguson, MO 63135

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Festus has one of the best small-town downtowns in the St. Louis metro — and a name with a story. It grew up next to the glass-factory town of Crystal City, and locals jointly call them the "Twin Cities." Festus was first nicknamed Tanglefoot (legend says for glass-plant workers whose feet tangled in the brush staggering home), then got the name Festus — supposedly when a preacher opened the Bible at random and landed on the name in the Book of Acts.
What matters today: there are no chains on Festus's Main Street. It's a genuinely walkable strip of independent restaurants, a brewery, a meadery, and bakeries. Here's where to eat in Festus.
Most of these sit on or just off Main Street , so park once and wander. (Heads-up: Truman Boulevard is the boundary with Crystal City — addresses there can land in either town, so this guide sticks to Festus-proper spots; for the Crystal City side, see that guide.) Time it for the Firecracker Festival in late June — carnival, drone show, and fireworks that draw tens of thousands.

### Pogolino's Pizza Place
Start with the anchor. Pogolino's has done family-owned thin-crust pizza and Italian since 1970 — fifty-plus years of crispy crust and specialty pies (the "Italian Stallion" among them) right on Main Street. The town's pizza institution.

### Petit Paree Restaurant & Lounge
The special-occasion room. Petit Paree has served French-inspired steak and seafood since 1960 — old-school lounge, white-tablecloth energy, a genuine Festus classic that's outlasted nearly everything.
📍 228 E Main St, Festus, MO 63028

### Main & Mill Brewing Company
Main & Mill is the downtown craft brewery and taproom that's become a true community hub — house beer, a friendly room, and a second "Central Tap" spot in town. The anchor of Festus's drinks scene.
📍 240 E Main St, Festus, MO 63028

### Taytro's Bar & Bistro
For something different, Taytro's brings "a taste of NOLA without leaving Missouri" — Cajun and Creole plates that have earned one of the strongest local followings in town. Just off Main, and worth the half-block.
📍 331 N Creek Dr, Festus, MO 63028

### The Brick Bistro & Brew
The Brick Bistro & Brew is the locally owned bistro-coffee-pizza combo (since 2018) — homemade soups, the "Popper" sandwich, thin-crust BBQ pizza, beer, and smoothies. The do-a-bit-of-everything daytime spot.
📍 218 E Main St, Festus, MO 63028

### Krabby Daddy's Seafood Eatery
Krabby Daddy's is the fast-casual Cajun seafood-boil spot — crab legs, shrimp, lobster, by the bag. It started right here in Festus (it's since grown, but this is the local original), and it scratches the seafood-boil itch the rest of Jefferson County can't.
📍 102 Pine St, Festus, MO 63028

### The Corner Cup Micro-Bakery
For the sweet stop, The Corner Cup is the cozy corner coffee-and-treats shop in a historic Main Street building — Kaldi's coffee, cupcakes, pies, hand pies, and scones, run by a local family. (Bread fan? The Braided Bakery a few doors down does challah, pretzels, and bagels a couple of days a week.)
📍 2 E Main St, Festus, MO 63028

### Why this little town matters
Festus is proof a small downtown can still be all its own — a Main Street with no chains, anchored by a 1970 pizza place, a 1960 French lounge, a craft brewery, a meadery, and a clutch of bakeries. That's a real local economy, the kind the national apps flatten into a list of interstate exits. We'd rather walk you down Main Street.

### FAQ
What's the oldest restaurant in Festus, MO?
Petit Paree (French-inspired steak and seafood, since 1960) and Pogolino's Pizza Place (family-owned since 1970) are the two longtime Main Street institutions.
Does Festus have a brewery?
Yes — Main & Mill Brewing Company on E Main Street, plus Four Brothers Mead (an award-winning meadery) downtown. The drinks scene is a real anchor of the no-chains Main Street.
Is Festus the same as Crystal City?
They're separate towns but physically continuous — locals call them the "Twin Cities." This guide covers Festus-proper spots; Crystal City has its own where-to-eat guide.
When is the Festus Firecracker Festival?
Late June — a carnival, drone show, and fireworks that draw tens of thousands downtown.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of North County — explore the whole region in our North County restaurant guide .
Florissant is the biggest city in St. Louis County, and one of the oldest places in the whole region — French settlers founded it around 1786, the Spanish called it St. Ferdinand, and the streets of Old Town still carry French names like Rue St. Denis and Rue St. Francois. Behind that colonial history is a genuinely good independent food scene, anchored by a 30-year landmark restaurant and one of the metro's most loved craft breweries.
From an 1873 building turned New American kitchen to a 24-hour donut shop, here's where to eat in Florissant.
The heart of it is Old Town Florissant (along the Rue streets and St. Francois), walkable and historic; a few favorites sit out on the Highway 67 corridor. A couple keep limited days, so check first. Time a spring trip for the Valley of Flowers Festival , Florissant's signature event the first full weekend of May since 1963.

### Hendel's Restaurant & Bar
Start at the flagship. Hendel's fills an 1873 brick building the Hendel family ran as a grocery and butcher shop until 1993 — now a New American restaurant run by the Bennett family for 30-plus years, with a custom oak bar and an estate wine list. The Cajun Carbonara is the signature. The anchor of Old Town dining.
📍 599 Rue St. Denis, Florissant, MO 63031

### Henke's Tavern
Henke's is a pre-Prohibition institution — the building started as an Anheuser-Busch “Bud bar” in the 1920s, became an ice cream parlor during Prohibition, and has been Henke's since 1955. Classic burgers and a true neighborhood-tavern feel, family-run.
📍 901 N Lafayette St, Florissant, MO 63031

### Florissant City Diner
Florissant City Diner is the veteran-owned classic — all-day-style breakfast and lunch, skillets and omelets, burgers, and an in-house bakery, with a regulars-as-family vibe (they sing happy birthday several times a week). The honest morning spot.
📍 1060 Rue St. Francois, Florissant, MO 63031

### Old Town Donuts
A St. Louis cult favorite, Old Town Donuts has been family-owned since 1968 — open 24 hours, with the old-fashioned sour cream cake donut as the one to get. Worth a late-night or early-morning detour.
📍 508 New Florissant Rd, Florissant, MO 63031

### Mann Meats
Mann Meats went from St. Louis Magazine's #1 food truck to a brick-and-mortar BBQ shop in Old Town — 10-to-12-hour smoked brisket, pork steaks, sauce on the side. A genuine pitmaster operation, family-owned.
📍 300 St. Ferdinand St, Florissant, MO 63031

### Costello's Pizzeria & Subs
The newest Old Town independent: brothers Mariano and Anthony Costello restored the historic Narrow Gauge railroad station house into a pizzeria (opened summer 2024) — St. Louis-style pizza, toasted ravioli, and hot subs, with a patio across from the frozen custard stand.
📍 1060 St. Catherine St, Florissant, MO 63031

### Cugino's Italian Bar & Grill
Out on the Highway 67 corridor, Cugino's (“cousins”) is the family-owned St. Louis-style Italian spot — pizza, pasta, and a sports-bar room. Fun local-history hook: Narrow Gauge Brewing was born in its basement in 2016 before opening its own taproom next door.
📍 1595 N US-67, Florissant, MO 63031

### Make it a day: Narrow Gauge Brewing
For craft beer, Narrow Gauge Brewing Co. (1545 N US-67) is one of the most acclaimed breweries in St. Louis — famous for hazy IPAs — now in a big standalone taproom after starting in Cugino's basement. The drinks anchor of a Florissant food crawl.

### Why this little town matters
Florissant is a 240-year-old French-and-Spanish colonial town hiding in plain sight in North County — and Old Town's independents prove it: an 1873-building restaurant, a pre-Prohibition tavern, a 1968 donut shop, a food-truck-champion pitmaster, and a railroad depot turned pizzeria. The national apps only show you the chains on the highway. We point you to the Rue streets.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in Florissant, MO?
Hendel's Restaurant & Bar in Old Town — a New American kitchen in an 1873 brick building, family-run for over 30 years, known for its Cajun Carbonara.
Where's the best BBQ in Florissant?
Mann Meats in Old Town — a former #1-rated St. Louis food truck now in a brick-and-mortar, doing 10-to-12-hour smoked brisket.
Is there a good brewery in Florissant?
Narrow Gauge Brewing Co. on Highway 67 — one of the most acclaimed craft breweries in St. Louis (famous for hazy IPAs), which started in the basement of Cugino's restaurant.
What's Old Town Florissant?
The city's historic district, with French-named streets (Rue St. Denis, Rue St. Francois) and Spanish/French colonial landmarks like Casa Alvarez (~1790) and Taille de Noyer — and most of the town's independent restaurants.

Foristell is a tiny town of about 550 straddling the St. Charles / Warren County line on I-70 — and most of its dining "volume" is the truck-stop cluster at Exit 203, which is all national chains. ### Taco Loco
The town's beloved independent — scratch-made Mexican in the small Main Street storefront that local favorite Sadie's used to fill. Birria tacos, bowls, homemade tortillas, and zesty salsas, pulling near-perfect reviews. Open daily.

### T & D Tavern
A classic American country tavern — hand-shaped, never-frozen burgers, fried pickles, and wings, with pool tables, cold cheap beer, and a renovated covered patio with live music. "Burgers, Brew and Good Friends Too." A bar first, but a real burger second.

### Renaissance Wine Garden
The destination curiosity — a winery with a two-story tree-house deck (it literally wraps a tree), a musical-instrument water fountain, an indoor art gallery, and a "Wine Lab" where you can blend and bottle your own. Wine, beer, and a food menu, weekends only (call ahead; weather-dependent).
📍 29131 N Stringtown Rd, Foristell, MO 63348

Foristell punches above its tiny size on dining volume — but only because of the I-70 chains. By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
About seven miles south of Belleville sits Freeburg — a little German village that started life in 1836 as "Urbana," then renamed itself in 1859 after Freiburg, in Baden , the homeland of the settlers who'd come for the cheap farmland and the coal under it. The mines shaped the town; the German families stuck around; and the result, generations later, is a Metro-East village where the restaurants tend to be old, family-owned, and exactly the kind of place you'd never find unless someone local told you.
So consider this someone local telling you. Freeburg fields a steakhouse that's been in one family since 1976, a from-scratch diner cooking since 1989, a brick-oven family grill, and a walk-up coffee bar that beats the gas-station cup every time. Here's where to eat in Freeburg.
Several of the best spots here are dinner-focused or keep limited days — the steakhouse is dinner-only and closed Mondays, and a couple of the others have hours that wander, so a quick call before you drive is smart. Come the third weekend in August and the whole town turns out for the Freeburg Homecoming & Rodeo at the rec park, now closing in on its 100th year — a parade, a carnival, a rodeo, and a fish fry to kick it off.

### Valentine's Restaurant
Start with the town's special-occasion spot. Valentine's has been a family-owned steakhouse since 1976 — coming up on fifty years of one family searing filet mignon (locals talk about the crust) and pouring a house blue cheese dressing people genuinely drive in for. Dinner only, closed Mondays. This is the anniversary-and-birthday room, and it's earned it.
📍 205 S State St, Freeburg, IL 62243

### Gary's Restaurant
For the other end of the day, Gary's has been cooking American home-style from scratch since 1989 — a classic family diner with a Saturday breakfast buffet and a Sunday lunch buffet that draw the after-church and the up-early crowds alike. Exactly the under-covered mom-and-pop a town this size lives on.
📍 405 S State St, Freeburg, IL 62243

### Reifschneider's Grill & Grape
Reifschneider's is the family-owned bar-and-grill carrying one of those unmistakably German Freeburg surnames — brick-oven pizza, steaks, seafood, burgers, and "award-winning wings," with live music nights and outdoor seating. The all-rounder where the whole family finds something, done by people whose name is on the building.
📍 700 N State St, Freeburg, IL 62243

### Tequila Mexican Restaurant
For the Mexican plate-and-margarita night, Tequila is the locally run sit-down spot — daily fresh salsa, street tacos, enchiladas, a real margarita list, and patio seating, at reasonable prices. The dependable independent option, not a chain in a sombrero.
📍 341 Marketplace Dr, Freeburg, IL 62243

### Next Up Sports Bar & Grill
When there's a game on, Next Up is the town's casual sports bar and grill — locally owned American pub fare with late hours Thursday through Saturday. The neighborhood game-day hang, and a newer addition to the lineup.
📍 301 Marketplace Dr, Freeburg, IL 62243

### The Coffee Pot
Skip the gas-station cup. The Coffee Pot is Freeburg's locally owned walk-up coffee bar — espresso, specialty drinks, and seasonal flavors poured fresh, the kind of independent caffeine stop a small town is lucky to have. It's a walk-up trailer concept, so think grab-and-go more than sit-and-stay, but the coffee's the real thing.
📍 210 N Main St, Freeburg, IL 62243

### Why this little town matters
Freeburg is a German coal-and-farm village most St. Louisans couldn't find on a map — and it quietly keeps a 1976 family steakhouse, a 1989 scratch diner, a brick-oven family grill, and a walk-up coffee bar all going at once. That's a town that decided, over and over, to keep its own places alive instead of surrendering to the franchise off the highway. The national apps will never tell that story; they'll just show you the chain logos.

What's the oldest restaurant in Freeburg, IL?
Valentine's Restaurant, a family-owned steakhouse since 1976 — known for its filet mignon and a much-requested house blue cheese dressing.

Gary's Restaurant, cooking from scratch since 1989, with a Saturday breakfast buffet and a Sunday lunch buffet. For coffee, The Coffee Pot is the local walk-up option.

The third weekend in August, at Freeburg Recreation Park — a long-running tradition now approaching its 100th year, with a parade, carnival, live music, and a rodeo.

### Grassi's Ristorante & Deli
The local independent. Grassi's has been a family-owned Italian counter-and-sit-down since 1968 — the Italian Salad was named the best in St. Louis by Sauce Magazine, and the chicken parmesan is a praised local classic. The kind of place where the salad alone built the reputation.
📍 10450 German Blvd, Frontenac, MO 63131

### Sugo's Spaghetteria
Sugo's is the pasta-focused spaghetteria run by the Del Pietro family (the same St. Louis Italian dynasty behind Babbo's) — spaghetti and meatballs is the house benchmark, with the Pomodoro a staple. A genuine local-family room, not a transplant.
📍 10419 Clayton Rd, Frontenac, MO 63131

### Mariposa (at Neiman Marcus)
Mariposa is the elegant lunch-only room inside Neiman Marcus at Plaza Frontenac — a genuine "ladies who lunch" institution surrounded by contemporary art, famous for its Mandarin orange soufflé. Open 11 a.m.–3 p.m. It's a department-store dining room (one-of-a-kind, not a chain), so we flag it honestly.
📍 100 Plaza Frontenac, St. Louis, MO 63131

### BrickTop's
BrickTop's is the upscale New American spot at Plaza Frontenac — prime steaks, fresh sushi, rotisserie chicken, and the famous deviled eggs over applewood bacon — with the see-and-be-seen patio of affluent West County. It's a Southern-based chain (labeled honestly), but it's a Plaza anchor.
📍 10342 Clayton Rd, Frontenac, MO 63131

### Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar
Fleming's is the prime steakhouse and wine bar on the south side of Plaza Frontenac — filet mignon, the cult chipotle-cheddar mac and cheese, and a roughly 100-wines-by-the-glass program. A national upscale chain, flagged as such — the steak-and-Cabernet pick.
📍 1855 S Lindbergh Blvd, Frontenac, MO 63131

### Brio Italian Grille
Brio is the Northern Italian grille at Plaza Frontenac — made-to-order pasta, wood-grilled flatbreads, steaks and chops, open seven days. A national Italian chain (labeled honestly), and the easy all-week Plaza option.
📍 1601 S Lindbergh Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63131

The independents cluster in a few walkable blocks of South Macoupin Street downtown (62033). Hours shift seasonally in small towns, so call ahead — a couple are dinner-only or closed Mondays. For more options, the Macoupin/coal-belt neighbors (Benld, Mt. Olive, Bunker Hill) are a short drive.

### Lumpy's Bar and Grill
The local favorite. Lumpy's is the downtown corner tavern where the weekly special board is the draw — fried chicken one night, pork fritter the next, plus Italian beef sandwiches and spaghetti with garlic bread. A 4.6-star regulars' room, lunch and dinner Tue–Sat.
📍 208 S Macoupin St, Gillespie, IL 62033

### Rocco's Italian Pizzeria
Rocco's is the dinner-only pizzeria locals call "best pie in town" — thin crust, Sicilian pan, St. Louis style, and Sicilian stuffed crust. That after-the-whistle, evening-only neighborhood-pizza feel. Closed Mondays.
📍 211 S Macoupin St, Gillespie, IL 62033

### Miners Family Restaurant
Miners is the all-day-breakfast family diner — chicken-fried steak, breakfast skillets, homemade chicken tenders — with a banquet room seating up to 70, so it's where the town gathers for big get-togethers. The name nods to Gillespie's coal-mining roots. Opens at 6 a.m.
📍 304 S Macoupin St, Gillespie, IL 62033

### Mi Casita
Mi Casita is the family-run Mexican spot punching above a town this size — street tacos, fajitas de camarón, chimichangas, margaritas and berry sangria, with a house "diablo sauce" reviewers love on the chips.
📍 101 E Walnut St, Gillespie, IL 62033

### China Garden
China Garden is the 27-year Chinese fixture on Macoupin Street — generous-portion Chinese-American standards that one regular calls the best Chinese in Macoupin County. Closed Mondays.
📍 203 S Macoupin St, Gillespie, IL 62033

### Why this town matters
Gillespie proves a 3,000-person coal town can eat well — a diner, a pizzeria, authentic Mexican, a Chinese kitchen, and a tavern-grill, all locally owned and walkable downtown, the heritage right there in "Miners Family Restaurant." Nobody writes about Gillespie's food. We do.

What's the best place to eat in Gillespie, IL?
Locals point to Lumpy's Bar and Grill (the weekly-special tavern) and Rocco's ("best pie in town") first. Miners Family Restaurant is the all-day-breakfast and home-cooking anchor.
Is there much to eat in a town this small?
Surprisingly, yes — for ~3,000 people, Gillespie has a diner, a pizzeria, authentic Mexican (Mi Casita), a Chinese kitchen (China Garden), and a tavern-grill, almost all on a few walkable blocks of South Macoupin Street.

Glen Carbon is stitched right onto Edwardsville — so tight the two share a Chamber of Commerce and a restaurant week. That means a lot of "Glen Carbon" results online are really Edwardsville spots a mile away. Glen Carbon's own scene is smaller but genuine: an Old Town pair of Main Street bars, a lunch-only tea room with a line, and trail-side custard and coffee. Skip the chain strip on Route 159 and head to Old Town.
From a smash-burger Main Street bar to a cabin with bourbon and live music, here's where to eat in Glen Carbon.
Glen Carbon's real independents are off the Route 159 chain corridor — clustered in Old Town on S. Main Street and along Glen Crossing Rd and Route 157 (62034). A few keep tight hours (the tea room is lunch-only; a couple close Mondays). And if you want more, Edwardsville's deeper scene is right next door.

### The Wooden Nickel Pub & Grill
The Wooden Nickel is the locally owned Old Town bar and grill with two patios and nine TVs — a smash burger, fried ravioli (the St. Louis-metro classic), and "nickel tacos." Kitchen runs lunch through evening while the bar stays late, so it's both a midday stop and a hang.
📍 171 S Main St, Glen Carbon, IL 62034

### Old Towne Tavern
Old Towne Tavern is the friendly Main Street dive a few doors down — hand-tossed fresh pizza is the calling card, with loaded nachos and burgers, a pool table, darts, and a heated patio. The easy neighborhood pub.
📍 155 S Main St, Glen Carbon, IL 62034

### Weeping Willow Tea Room
Weeping Willow is the from-scratch lunch tea room so popular it won't take reservations — daily homemade soups, generous specialty sandwiches, and scratch desserts. Show up by 11:30 or expect a wait. A genuine little gem.
📍 123 Glen Crossing Rd, Glen Carbon, IL 62034

### The Cabin at Judy Creek
The Cabin at Judy Creek is the cabin-style craft bar with 14 taps, a deep bourbon list, and live music every weekend — plus a small scratch menu where the smoked tri-tip panini is the one reviewers name first. A stay-a-while spot.
📍 3730 S State Rte 157, Glen Carbon, IL 62034

### Annie's Frozen Custard
Annie's is the year-round local custard window with a drive-thru — fresh frozen custard, concretes, and sundaes, open into the evening. The default after-game, after-trail family stop.
📍 11 Illini Dr, Glen Carbon, IL 62034

### Goshen Coffee Roasters
Goshen is the homegrown 618-area coffee roaster (a small local chain, not a national one) — it roasts its own beans, with house espresso drinks, cinnamon rolls, scones, and loaded breakfast burritos, a sunny patio, and a drive-thru. The local-roast morning stop.
📍 1 Junction Dr W, Glen Carbon, IL 62034

### Why this town matters
Glen Carbon is small and shares a food scene with Edwardsville — but the Old Town bars, the lunch-only tea room, and the trail-side custard and coffee are genuinely its own. Glendale is one of St. Louis County's smallest cities — 1.2 square miles, about 6,200 people, founded in 1912 as a summer-home retreat and almost entirely residential. There's no commercial downtown, so its in-limits food comes down to two genuine spots on North Sappington Road: a beloved coffee shop and an old-school deli-grocery. The good news? Glendale is wedged between two of the metro's best food towns, so a great meal is five minutes away in any direction. People here get hungry too — here are the local two, plus the closest favorites.
From a latte across from City Hall to a 1956 thin-crust pizza, here's where to eat in (and right around) Glendale.
Glendale's two in-limits spots sit on North Sappington Road (63122). Heads up: 63122 is a Kirkwood ZIP, so listings often mis-tag Glendale addresses as "Kirkwood" or "St. Louis." Both local spots are daytime/casual — no full-service dinner restaurant exists inside Glendale. For dinner and more variety, Kirkwood, Webster Groves, and Rock Hill are all 5–10 minutes away.

### The Glendale Grind
The town's coffee house — handcrafted espresso drinks and fresh-baked pastries, sweet and savory, with outdoor seating. It sits directly across from Glendale City Hall in the literal center of town, and the city's own page welcomed it as "Glendale's newest business." The neighborhood's morning anchor.
📍 421 N Sappington Rd, Glendale, MO 63122

### Hanneke's Westwood Grocery, Deli & Catering
A genuine throwback corner grocery-with-a-deli-counter — fresh-cut meats and made-to-order sandwiches like the Tom Boy Club, the Summit (roast beef on toasted French bread), and the warm multi-meat Monty, plus hearty chef salads and St. Louis-style pizza. The place Glendale residents grab lunch or order catering.
📍 190 N Sappington Rd, Glendale, MO 63122

### Closest favorites a few minutes away
Glendale sits between two foodie towns, so dinner is never far — these are the closest distinctive independents:
- Kirkwood (Old Kirkwood / Argonne): Billy G's (American-Italian, big patio) and One 19 North (tapas and wine bar).
- Webster Groves (Old Webster / Old Orchard): Big Sky Cafe (farm-to-table) and Cyrano's (legendary desserts and martinis).
- Rock Hill (Manchester Rd): Farotto's (family pizza since 1956) and the old-school Charcoal House steakhouse.

Godfrey sits on the bluffs just north of Alton, a Riverbend town on the Great River Road with a community college and a surprising number of genuine independents. Most "Godfrey restaurant" lists online quietly pad themselves with Alton spots a few minutes south — but Godfrey holds its own, anchored by one of the only true farm-to-table kitchens in the entire Metro East. Skip the assumption that you have to drive to Alton; Godfrey eats well on its own.
From a garden-to-plate destination to a fresh-flavor-a-day custard window, here's where to eat in Godfrey.
Godfrey's spots spread along Godfrey Road, Delmar Avenue, and the Montclaire area (62035), tied together by the Great River Road scenic byway and Lewis & Clark Community College. A couple close Mondays or Tuesdays, and a few close early — and if you want still more, Alton's bigger downtown is a 5–10 minute drive.

### Bakers & Hale
The destination. Bakers & Hale is one of the only true farm-to-table restaurants in the St. Louis Metro East — they grow a lot of their own vegetables and herbs in an on-site garden, on the wooded north end of Godfrey. New American plates like burnt-ends mac and cheese and smoked pork belly, with gooey butter cake to finish.
📍 7120 Montclaire Ave, Godfrey, IL 62035

### Delmar Public House
Delmar Public House perches atop the Godfrey bluffs with an unexpected globe-spanning menu — chicken tikka masala next to falafel next to cottage pie — that you can pair with a draught beer or a martini. One of the area's newer arrivals and a fun mix.
📍 2926 West Delmar Ave, Godfrey, IL 62035

### Joe's Pizza & Pasta
Joe's has served Godfrey since 2017 on the Trupiano family's own secret recipes — the dough and sauces trace back to the family, not a corporate spec sheet. The Trupiano Carbonara is the move. It's a small family group with a few Metro East sisters, still family-run.
📍 5775 Godfrey Rd, Ste A, Godfrey, IL 62035

### Carver's Southern-Style BBQ
Carver's smokes its pork shoulder over hickory and pulls it by hand — that's the stated specialty — alongside beef brisket and burnt ends that sell only until they run out. Southern-style barbecue, so come early for the burnt ends.
📍 2716 Grovelin St, Godfrey, IL 62035

### Round Table Family Restaurant
Round Table is the family-owned booth-and-coffee diner where breakfast runs all day from 6 a.m. and the regulars have a usual — daily specials and classic comfort plates. The everyday American spot.
📍 5407 Godfrey Rd, Ste B, Godfrey, IL 62035

### Germania Brew Haus
Germania Brew Haus is a homegrown local coffee brand whose Godfrey location runs a busy drive-thru and added a rooftop and walk-up space in spring 2026 — espresso drinks, smoothies, and teas. The local coffee stop.
📍 5775 Godfrey Rd, Ste F, Godfrey, IL 62035

### Shivers Frozen Custard
Shivers churns its custard fresh daily with a different flavor of the day, every day — concretes, sundaes, and shakes, open as late as 11 p.m. on weekends. The classic after-dinner Godfrey Road stop.
📍 3318 Godfrey Rd, Godfrey, IL 62035

Godfrey gets written off as "just drive to Alton," but it's got a genuine farm-to-table destination, a bluff-top global pub, family Italian, hand-pulled barbecue, and a fresh-daily custard window of its own. Bakers & Hale — billed as one of the only true farm-to-table restaurants in the entire Metro East, growing its own produce on-site. It's the spot that makes Godfrey a destination, not just everyday eats.
Is Godfrey's food scene just part of Alton's?
They're tied together in the Riverbend, and many online lists pad "Godfrey" with Alton spots — but Godfrey has a real roster of its own (Bakers & Hale, Delmar Public House, Joe's, Carver's). Alton's bigger downtown is a 5–10 minute drive for more.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Grafton is the oldest city in Jersey County, perched where the Illinois River pours into the Mississippi — a tiny river-tourism town of about 600 people on the Great River Road. It's the "Winter Home of the Bald Eagle," gateway to Illinois's largest state park (Pere Marquette), and home to a gondola SkyTour that lifts you 300 feet up the bluff for the best river view in the region. The 1993 flood reshaped the town, but it came back as a wine-and-river-deck destination.
For a town this small, the food-and-drink scene is all character. Here's where to eat in Grafton.
It's a small, seasonal river town — most spots have deck/patio seating and run extended hours in the warm months, lighter in winter (when the eagles arrive). The wineries and the SkyTour are the marquee draws; pair them with a meal. (Elsah is a separate village a few miles east — this guide stays in Grafton proper.)

### The Grafton Winery & Brewhaus
Start with the anchor. The Grafton Winery & Brewhaus is a full-production winery and microbrewery with an on-site restaurant — dry-to-sweet wines, seasonal brews, and smoked meats, downtown on Main Street. The town's go-to for a glass and a plate.
📍 300 W Main St, Grafton, IL 62037

### Grafton Harbor & the Oyster Bar
Grafton Harbor is a marina with a floating winery and the Grafton Oyster Bar — Cajun-Creole and fresh seafood (char-grilled oysters, shrimp po'boy, jambalaya) served literally on the water, with live music on summer weekends. The only floating restaurant in the Midwest.
📍 215 W Water St, Grafton, IL 62037

### Aerie's Resort & Winery
For the view of all views, Aerie's is the bluff-top winery and terrace restaurant — reached by the Grafton SkyTour gondola (~300 feet up) — overlooking the Illinois/Mississippi confluence. The wine and the panorama are the point; the ride up is half the fun.
📍 14 W Main St (SkyTour base), Grafton, IL 62037

### The Loading Dock Bar & Grill
The Loading Dock is the big riverfront American bar-and-grill — burgers, sandwiches, and salads on a multi-level deck "next to the Mighty Mississippi," with live music and seasonal events. The lively group hang.
📍 401 E Front St, Grafton, IL 62037

### O'Jan's Fish Stand
O'Jan's is the beloved no-frills fish stand right on the river — made-to-order fried fish sandwiches, plus burgers and pork tenderloins. A walk-up river classic and the quick-bite move.
📍 101 W Main St, Grafton, IL 62037

### The Hawg Pit BBQ Barn
The Hawg Pit is the landmark BBQ joint and self-styled "best biker bar in the Riverbend" — smoked meats, cold beer, live music, and Mississippi views. A riverside institution that draws motorcycle and car clubs.
📍 821 W Main St, Grafton, IL 62037

### Fountain Hill Steak & Seafood
The comeback story: Fountain Hill opened in 2025 in the old Fin Inn building, keeping the beloved table-side aquarium windows for nostalgia while adding steaks, fresh seafood (catfish, walleye), and Sunday brunch. A loss turned into a revival.
📍 1500 W Main St, Grafton, IL 62037

### Why this little town matters
Grafton is a 600-person river town that lives entirely on character — wineries, a floating oyster bar, a bluff-top gondola restaurant, a biker BBQ barn, and the revived Fin Inn aquariums — at the spot where two great rivers meet. There's not a chain in its core, and the national apps can't capture the deck-and-confluence magic. We can.

### FAQ
What's the best riverfront dining in Grafton, IL?
Grafton Harbor's floating Oyster Bar (seafood literally on the water) and Aerie's bluff-top winery terrace (reached by the SkyTour gondola) for the view; The Loading Dock for a lively deck.
What happened to the Fin Inn in Grafton?
The Fin Inn closed, but in 2025 Fountain Hill Steak & Seafood opened in the building — keeping the famous table-side aquarium windows and adding steaks, seafood, and Sunday brunch.
Does Grafton have wineries?
Yes — The Grafton Winery & Brewhaus (also a microbrewery), Grafton Harbor's floating winery, and Aerie's Resort & Winery up the bluff.
What's there to do in Grafton besides eat?
The Grafton SkyTour gondola, winter bald-eagle watching, Pere Marquette State Park (Illinois's largest) just west, and the confluence of the Illinois and Mississippi Rivers.
