You're an hour southwest of the city on I-44, climbing the ridge between the Meramec and the Bourbeuse, when two water towers come into view — one marked HOT , the other COLD , side by side, the town's deadpan little joke on itself. That's St. Clair: a genuine Route 66 town that's never taken itself too seriously, and one that quietly feeds travelers better than the interstate exits let on.
This is Mother Road country, where a family café has been slinging pie since 1938 and the newer spots — crepes, craft cocktails, real Mexican — have set up shop without running the old ones off. Pull off at exit 239 or 240 and here's where to eat in St. Clair.
St. Clair splits between the old downtown on Main Street and the service roads along I-44 , so you'll do a little driving between stops. Lewis Café's pies are first-come, first-served, and a couple of the bar-and-grills keep evening-only hours — worth a check before you go. Time it for the Waterfront Beer, Wine & Cocktail Festival if you want the town at full pour.

### Lewis Café
Start at the heart of it. Lewis Café has anchored Main Street since 1938 — a classic American diner where breakfast runs all day and the homemade pies (coconut cream, lemon meringue) are the reason Route 66 travelers have been pulling off here for generations. It's been family-run for decades, and it tastes like it.
📍 145 S Main St, St. Clair, MO 63077

### Gibby's
Gibby's has been the community's casual go-to since 2010 — burgers and proper St. Louis-style pizza in a sit-down family room right off the old road. Nothing fancy, everything solid; the kind of place a small town actually eats at on a Tuesday.

### Roots Cafe
For the morning, Roots Cafe is the bright modern spot doing made-to-order sweet and savory crepes , toasted paninis, homemade soups, and a real coffee-and-espresso program. A genuinely good café in an I-44 town is a small miracle — this one earns it.

### Buenas Vibras Mexican Restaurant
When you want tacos and a margarita, Buenas Vibras is the family-owned Mexican spot on the service road — tacos, fajita nachos, chimichangas, enchiladas, with vegetarian options and the good kind of casual buzz. Independent, generous, and open late most nights.

### Blondie's Breezeway Kitchen & Cocktails
The locals' tucked-away favorite, Blondie's Breezeway is a kitchen-and-cocktail spot just off Main with a balcony patio (the "Breezeway") that's the whole point on a nice night. Owner-run, locally praised, and a little more grown-up than the standard small-town bar.

### Scarlett's Bar & Grill

St. John is a tiny half-square-mile municipality, and its food lives almost entirely on one stretch of St. Charles Rock Road. ### Chuck-A-Burger Drive-In
The St. John legend. Chuck-A-Burger is the last surviving location of a drive-in chain that had eight spots around St. Louis in the 1960s — still doing real curb service (you eat in your car, no dining room) since 1957. Burgers and curly fries, a homemade cherry Coke, and chili made from the original 1957 recipe that's won multiple cook-offs. Seasonal classic-car cruise nights fill the lot. Closed Sundays.
📍 9025 St Charles Rock Rd, St. John, MO 63114

### El Comal (just west in Overland)
A minute west on the Rock Road, El Comal is a locally owned Mexican-and-Honduran spot with a full bar — torta al pastor, sopes, a house spicy green salsa, plus rare-for-the-area Honduran plates like montañas, maduros, and pollo con tajadas. Distinctive and generous.

### Mi Hungry BBQ & Jamaican Cuisine (Overland)
Also just west, Mi Hungry is a family-owned Jamaican-and-BBQ spot — jerk and oxtail-style plates and barbecue, an authentic Caribbean option that's genuinely rare in North County.
📍 8660 St Charles Rock Rd, Overland, MO 63114

### Big Jay's Fish, Chicken & Shrimp (Breckenridge Hills)
Just east on the Rock Road, Big Jay's is the locally owned Southern fish-and-soul-food counter — fried jack salmon, catfish, whiting, wings, and shrimp baskets. The classic North County fish-and-chicken fix.
📍 9701 St Charles Rock Rd, Breckenridge Hills, MO 63114

### Why this town matters
St. John is tiny, and its one true claim is a big one — the last Chuck-A-Burger, a genuine 1957 drive-in landmark that carries the whole "local in St. John" story on its own. Around it, the shared ZIP means the closest authentic independents are technically in Overland and Breckenridge Hills. The honest move is to name the real one in town and route you to the genuine spots a minute away — which is exactly what this page does.
Search St Louis Near Me Directory for St. John and North County before you go — and our Overland guide and St. Ann guide cover the deeper Rock Road scene minutes away.
And if you run a St. John spot — a drive-in, a taqueria, a fish counter — a listing is how the next North County neighbor finds you .

### FAQ
What's the best place to eat in St. John, MO?
Chuck-A-Burger Drive-In on St. Charles Rock Road — the last surviving location of a 1957 St. Louis drive-in chain, still doing real car-hop curb service with a cook-off-winning chili recipe. It's the genuine local landmark in town.
Why are there so few restaurants in St. John?
St. John is a tiny half-square-mile city, and its 63114 ZIP is shared with Overland and Breckenridge Hills — so most "St. John" listings are actually those neighbors. The St. John core is the 8900–9090 block of St. Charles Rock Road.
Where's the closest independent food to St. John?
Just over the line: El Comal (Mexican-Honduran) and Mi Hungry (Jamaican-BBQ) a minute west in Overland, and Big Jay's (Southern fish and soul food) just east in Breckenridge Hills. Our Overland guide has more.

### Plan your St. John visit
A 1957-recipe chili dog and curly fries in your car at Chuck-A-Burger, then Honduran plates at El Comal or jerk at Mi Hungry just down the road. For more local spots across North County, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

From cocktails to fine dining, a sandwich to lobster, a rooftop bar to takeout Asian — here's where to eat in and around downtown St. Louis. If you're in town for business, a Cardinals or City SC game, a Blues night, or a show at the Fox, every one of these is a walk or a short Lyft from the convention center, the stadiums, Union Station, and Ballpark Village. Forty-one spots, from a Soulard dive to a bourbon-bar steakhouse, an oyster bar to a Filipino kitchen.
Pick your block and your mood — here's the downtown St. Louis map.
These are grouped by walkable pocket: Busch Stadium / Ballpark Village , the downtown core / Washington Avenue , Union Station & Market Street , Midtown (Olive–Locust–Chouteau) , Lafayette Square , Soulard , Benton Park , and a few a short ride out (Central West End / Midtown). All are in the City of St. Louis; a few keep limited or late hours, so call ahead.

📍 601 Clark Ave, St. Louis, MO 63102

### FAQ
Where should I eat near Busch Stadium or Ballpark Village?
Broadway Oyster Bar (Cajun and live music), Katie's Pizza & Pasta and Condado Tacos in Ballpark Village, and 360 Rooftop Bar atop the Hilton for skyline-and-stadium views — all a short walk from the ballpark.
Where's a good downtown St. Louis dinner before a show at the Fox or a Blues game?
For fine dining, Hamilton's Urban Steakhouse, Blood & Sand, or Carmine's; for something lively, Polite Society or Eleven Eleven Mississippi in Lafayette Square; for BBQ, Pappy's Smokehouse in Midtown.
Where can I get lobster, or a great sandwich, downtown?
Peacemaker Lobster & Crab (Benton Park) for lobster rolls and crab boils; Mound City Sandwich Shop, Sauce on the Side (calzones), or Pickles Deli for sandwiches.
What's open late or good for a group downtown?
North Outpost is a late-night scratch kitchen; Soulard bars like Big Daddy's and The Great Grizzly Bear, plus 4 Hands Brewing and Square One Brewery, are easy for groups.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Let's be honest: St. Peters is chain country. The Mid Rivers Mall Drive corridor is a wall of Applebee's, Arby's, Chick-fil-A, and Wingstop. But the genuine locally owned spots are here and worth the detour — award-winning fried chicken served inside an American Legion hall, a husband-and-wife shop where she makes the cakes and he runs the taco line, and a certified-Neapolitan pizzeria you book a month out.
From a Legion-hall fried chicken legend to a married couple's taco-and-cake shop, here's where to eat in St. Peters.
The independents are scattered off the chain corridor — Historic Old Town (Hobo's on Main) and the Jungermann Road cluster (Erio's, Golden Chicken). Watch the unusual closed days: Golden Chicken is closed Thursdays, Erio's Sundays, Rosy's & Paco's Sunday and Monday. Use "St. Peters" (Google often says "Saint Peters").

### Hobo's At The Legion
Ask any local and this name comes up first. Hobo's is the family-run scratch kitchen tucked inside the American Legion Post 313 hall in Historic Old Town — award-winning fried chicken (voted Best in St. Charles County) and crispy fish platters, going strong for 18-plus years. The town's worst-kept secret.
📍 200 Main Street, St. Peters, MO 63376

### Erio's Ristorante
Erio's has held local loyalty for 25-plus years — Sicilian recipes from born-in-Sicily founder Pietro Pullizzi, who moved the restaurant from Florissant to St. Peters in 1991. Mussels Pomodoro and toasted ravioli are the orders. Closed Sundays.
📍 951 Jungermann Rd, St. Peters, MO 63376

### Rosy's Cakes & Paco's Tacos
Rosy's & Paco's is the married-couple shop with a rare double identity — Rosy is the cake artist, Paco the taquero — so you can grab authentic street tacos and a custom Mexican dessert under one roof. Feast Magazine calls them some of the most talented Mexican-food makers in the area.
📍 6240 Mexico Rd, St. Peters, MO 63376

### Lil' Mickey's Memphis Barbeque
Lil' Mickey's is the no-frills Memphis-style barbecue spot — chopped beef brisket cooked nearly to shredding, pork-shoulder sandwiches, and rib tips, all under a signature house sauce. As the Post-Dispatch put it, it got bigger but kept its soul.
📍 1020 Cave Springs Blvd, St. Peters, MO 63376

### Golden Chicken
Golden Chicken is the from-scratch Mediterranean and Middle Eastern spot that stands out in a corridor of fast-food chicken — shawarma, whole rotisserie chicken, and crispy falafel made fresh daily. Just note: closed Thursdays.
📍 632 Jungermann Rd, St. Peters, MO 63376

### Kasabi Japanese Steakhouse & Ramen
Kasabi is the newer independent right by Mid Rivers Mall doing the full tableside hibachi show, plus sushi and ramen bowls — a genuine local alternative to the chain hibachi spots.
📍 258 Mid Rivers Center, St. Peters, MO 63376

### Noto Italian Restaurant
Noto is the chef-driven destination — certified Neapolitan pizza and house-made pasta (nduja pizza, lobster ravioli) — and it's reservation-only, dinner Wednesday through Saturday, booking up to 30 days out. Plan ahead; it's worth it.
📍 5105 Westwood Dr, Ste B, St. Peters, MO 63304

### Why this town matters
St. Peters is exactly the kind of chain-dominated suburb where a local guide earns its keep — the genuine independents are scattered off the mall corridor, in a Legion hall and a strip-mall pizzeria you'd never find from the highway. The apps push the franchises; we point you to the fried chicken locals actually drive for.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in St. Peters, MO?
Locals point to Hobo's At The Legion — award-winning fried chicken inside the American Legion hall in Old Town. For a destination dinner, Noto Italian (certified Neapolitan, reservation-only).
Is St. Peters all chain restaurants?
The Mid Rivers Mall Dr corridor is heavily chain (Applebee's, Arby's, Chick-fil-A, Wingstop), but there's a real bench of independents off the strip — Hobo's, Erio's, Rosy's & Paco's, Lil' Mickey's, Golden Chicken.
Watch the closed days — which spots close mid-week?
Golden Chicken is closed Thursdays, Erio's is closed Sundays, and Rosy's & Paco's is closed Sunday and Monday. Call ahead.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
About an hour south of St. Louis down the Great River Road sits Missouri's oldest town — Ste. Genevieve, founded by French colonists around 1735, with the densest collection of French colonial vertical-log houses in North America and its own unit of the National Park System. It's a genuine day-trip destination: cobbled history, a Mississippi River ferry to Illinois, wine country in the hills, and a downtown of long-running independent restaurants and saloons.
Worth the drive for the history, and worth staying for the food. Here's where to eat in Ste. Genevieve.
It's about 60 miles south of St. Louis via I-55 / the Great River Road — a true day trip. The restaurants cluster in the historic downtown (Main, Merchant, 3rd Streets); a couple keep limited days (one's Thursday–Saturday only), so check first. Time it for Jour de Fête (a huge August crafts fair), the June French Heritage Festival , or the New Year's La Guignolée caroling tradition.

### Audubon's Grill & Bar
Start downtown. Audubon's is the upscale-casual anchor — scratch-made plates spanning French, Cajun, German, and Italian, in a building that's anchored the town's social scene since 1901 (with a boutique hotel upstairs). Named for naturalist John James Audubon, who lived here around 1811.
📍 9 N Main St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### The Old Brick House
The Old Brick House serves American comfort food in one of the oldest brick buildings west of the Mississippi — a genuine local institution and a fitting place to eat in the country's French-colonial cradle.
📍 90 S 3rd St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Anvil Restaurant & Saloon
The Anvil is the historic saloon-and-grill, established 1855 , with a back bar said to have come from an 1850s Mississippi River shipwreck. Famous onion rings, fried chicken, and pork tenderloin, plus Sunday breakfast. Pure river-town history on a plate.
📍 46 S 3rd St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Sirro's
Sirro's is the casual, ~30-year town favorite — 30-plus "samiches," pizza, pasta, burgers, homemade onion rings, and a salad bar. The dependable, feed-the-whole-family spot.
📍 261 Merchant St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Stella & Me Cafe
Stella & Me is the cozy lunch café in the arts district — sandwiches, salads, and light bites among rustic hardwood and local art. The charming midday stop.
📍 198 N Main St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Oliver's
Oliver's is the family-owned spot making fresh pasta by hand every morning , plus soups, salads, and sandwiches. Limited hours (Thursday–Saturday), so plan around it — but the from-scratch pasta is worth it.
📍 109 N Main St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Birdies Coffee + Bakery
For the morning, Birdies is the woman-owned coffee-and-bakery — scratch coffee, matcha, and pastries, with a drive-thru and walk-up. (It took over a long-running coffee corner downtown.)
📍 122 N Main St, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Charleville Vineyard, Winery & Microbrewery
For wine country, Charleville is the destination just outside town — handcrafted wines and house beer since 2003, a big tasting room with a self-serve tap wall, fire-pit patios, and a refurbished 1860s log-cabin lodge. The "make a day of it" cap (it's a short drive into the county hills).
📍 16937 Boyd Rd, Ste. Genevieve, MO 63670

### Why this little town matters
Ste. Genevieve is the rare place where the history is the destination — Missouri's oldest town, a National Historical Park of French colonial log houses — and the food has the same deep roots: an 1855 saloon, one of the oldest brick buildings in the West turned restaurant, a winery-brewery in the hills. That's a day trip the national apps can't plan for you. We can.

### FAQ
Is Ste. Genevieve worth the drive from St. Louis for food?
Yes — it's about an hour south, Missouri's oldest town, with a National Historical Park of French colonial houses and a downtown of long-running independents (Audubon's, the 1855 Anvil Saloon, the Old Brick House) plus wine country. A genuine day trip.
What's the most historic place to eat in Ste. Genevieve?
The Anvil Restaurant & Saloon (established 1855, with a shipwreck back bar) and The Old Brick House (one of the oldest brick buildings west of the Mississippi).
Is there a winery near Ste. Genevieve?
Yes — Charleville Vineyard, Winery & Microbrewery, a short drive into the county hills, making both wine and beer since 2003.
What festivals does Ste. Genevieve have?
Jour de Fête (a large August crafts fair), the June French Heritage Festival, La Guignolée (New Year's French caroling), and the February King's Ball.

History downtown, onion rings at the 1855 Anvil, hand-made pasta at Oliver's, and wine at Charleville in the hills. For more local spots across the region, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Sullivan sits right on Interstate 44 — old Route 66 — the gateway town for Meramec Caverns and Meramec State Park, where Lester Dill's painted-barn billboards once lined the Mother Road. People pour off the highway here for the caves and the river, and the good news is the town feeds them like it means it: a scratch café-bakery, a steakhouse pushing seventy years, and a veteran-owned brewery smoking its own BBQ.
When you're out here for the caverns, the fair, or just a break from the interstate, here's where to eat in Sullivan.
The independents cluster on North Clark Street downtown and along the service roads off I-44. A few keep early or limited hours (the cafés close mid-afternoon; the smokehouse is Tuesday–Saturday), so check before you go. Time it for the Meramec Community Fair in June — five days of parade, rodeo, and midway food at the fairgrounds.

### Clark Street Cafe & Bakery
Start downtown. Clark Street Cafe & Bakery is the family-owned scratch café — homemade soups, quiche, salads, sandwiches, fresh-baked goods, and fresh-roasted coffee. The quiche-with-biscuits-and-gravy and the California Club are the orders; it's the stylish hometown spot for breakfast and lunch. Closed Sundays.
📍 111 N Clark St, Sullivan, MO 63080

### Silo Restaurant
The local landmark. Silo has been a family-owned American restaurant since 1961 (old-timers still call it by its former name, the Du Kum Inn) — steaks, a weekend homemade breakfast buffet, and bread pudding, with 60-plus years of Sullivan history in the room. The special-occasion spot.
📍 200 S Service Rd W, Sullivan, MO 63080

### Muddy Banks Brewing Co.
The newer reason to stop. Muddy Banks is a veteran-owned craft brewery with a smoked-meat kitchen — house beer paired with brisket, pulled pork, and the rest, on a patio. The only brewery in town, and a genuinely good one.
📍 725 Acid Mine Rd, Sullivan, MO 63080

### MK BBQ
More smoke downtown: MK BBQ on North Clark is the family-owned smokehouse putting out brisket, smoked ribs, and pulled chicken — takeout, dine-in, and dog-friendly. The everyday BBQ fix.
📍 202 N Clark St, Sullivan, MO 63080

### Our Story Coffee House
Our Story Coffee House is the independent coffee-and-bakery spot (with an attached home-and-gift store) — locally loved coffee and pastries, and a real community gathering place. The morning anchor.
📍 454 N Church St, Sullivan, MO 63080

### Poppy Co.
The fun newcomer, Poppy Co. does dirty sodas, specialty coffee, energy drinks, and light bites — with a little shop and a kids' play area. A family-friendly modern café on Clark Street; a bright pause between cave trips.
📍 217 N Clark St, Sullivan, MO 63080

### Need it quick? A local burger to know
If you just want a fast burger, Rich's Famous Burgers (101 Grande Center Dr) does handmade burgers and is a small Missouri family operation (also in Pacific) — a local favorite rather than a national chain. Beyond that, the I-44 interchange has the usual fast-food lineup.

### Why this little town matters
Sullivan is a Route 66 town most people only meet on the way to the caves — but it keeps a 1961 steakhouse, a scratch café-bakery, a veteran-owned brewery, and a downtown smokehouse all going, plus the painted-barn Mother Road history right outside. The national apps reduce all of that to the fast-food logos at the exit. We'd rather point you to the real ones.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in Sullivan, MO?
For an occasion, the Silo (a family steakhouse since 1961). For breakfast or lunch, Clark Street Cafe & Bakery. For beer and BBQ, the veteran-owned Muddy Banks Brewing.
Is Sullivan a good Route 66 / Meramec Caverns food stop?
Yes — it's the gateway town to Meramec Caverns and Meramec State Park, with a genuine lineup of local independents downtown, not just interstate chains.
Where's the BBQ in Sullivan?
Two spots: Muddy Banks Brewing (veteran-owned brewery + smokehouse) and MK BBQ on North Clark Street.
When is the Meramec Community Fair?
Five days each June at the Sullivan fairgrounds — parade, rodeo, truck-and-tractor pull, livestock auction, carnival, and concerts.

Sunset Hills sits where Lindbergh meets Watson Road just off I-44, and its dining spine runs right through the middle of that intersection. The catch is the ZIP code blur — cross a block and you're in Crestwood or Sappington — so plenty of "Sunset Hills" spots technically aren't. The genuine ones are a fun mix: a tableside-cart steakhouse, a 2005 family sushi bar, an all-vegan café, and a chef-built burger counter hiding inside a gas station.
From a batter-dipped lobster tail to a gas-station smash burger worth the stop, here's where to eat in Sunset Hills.
The dining runs along Lindbergh Blvd and Watson Rd (63127), but ZIPs blur fast — a block off and you're in Crestwood (63126) or Sappington (63128). We've kept to verified 63127 spots. A few close Sundays or Mondays. For more, downtown Kirkwood is five minutes north.

### Twisted Tree Steakhouse
The marquee. Twisted Tree is the upscale independent steakhouse at Watson and Lindbergh — aged Creekstone Black Angus, a signature batter-dipped lobster tail, and tableside cart service, a throwback touch backed by two veteran St. Louis restaurant families. The date-night room. Closed Sunday and Monday.
📍 10701 Watson Rd, Sunset Hills, MO 63127

### Tokyo Sushi
Tokyo Sushi has been family-owned since 2005 — the house "Sunset Hills Roll," a full nigiri and sashimi list, plus udon and teriyaki for non-sushi eaters. The neighborhood sushi fixture that's outlasted nearly every chain on the strip.
📍 3729 S Lindbergh Blvd, Sunset Hills, MO 63127

### The Brothers Beer & Bourbon House
The Brothers is the cozy beer-and-bourbon bar with a small-plates kitchen — tacos, sliders, wings, and nachos alongside a rotating wall of ~250–300 beers and ~100 bourbons that changes weekly. A low-key date or buddies' night.
📍 3880 S Lindbergh Blvd, Ste 300, Sunset Hills, MO 63127

### El Agave Mexican Restaurant
El Agave is the full-bar Mexican-and-seafood spot tucked into Sunset Hills Plaza — fresh mains and Mexican-style mariscos, an easy sit-down among the big-box stores.
📍 10893 Sunset Hills Plaza, Sunset Hills, MO 63127

### Plant Craft Kitchen
Plant Craft Kitchen is chef-owner Rachel Carr's all-vegan café — it grew out of a 2020 meal-prep delivery business into a brick-and-mortar doing chef-driven plant-based bowls and prepared meals. A genuinely rare all-vegan option in a steak-and-burger corridor.
📍 3860 S Lindbergh Blvd #105, Sunset Hills, MO 63127

### Shelly's Smashburgers
Shelly's is the don't-judge-it-by-the-sign spot — a genuinely good chef-built burger counter inside a Phillips 66 , run by Mathew Unger (former exec chef at the Missouri Athletic Club). Get the Shelly's Double and the bacon-cheddar "tater keg" tots.
📍 4504 S Lindbergh Blvd, Sunset Hills, MO 63127

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Swansea is a small St. Clair County town pressed right up against Belleville's west side, and its main drag — North Illinois Street (Route 159) — is a classic Metro East chain corridor. You'll pass Applebee's, Outback, and a wall of fast food before you spot the local spots. But the genuine independents are here and surprisingly varied: in-house-butchered American, fresh-made Mexican, scratch Indian, a chef-driven smash-burger campus, and a Friday-only fried-fish window that's a true local ritual.
From a brick-oven cracklin'-crust pizza to a one-day-a-week fish stand, here's where to eat in Swansea.
Most of Swansea's independents sit on or just off North Illinois Street (Route 159) (62226), threaded between the chains. Watch the quirky-hours spots: the fish stand is Friday and cash only, Soulcial closes Sundays. And because Swansea and Belleville are basically one dining scene, neighboring Belleville's downtown adds far more locally owned options minutes away.

### Fletcher's Kitchen & Tap
Fletcher's is the family-owned American grill (the Swansea location of the local Fletcher's, going since 2004) that butchers its beef, chicken, and seafood in-house and rolls its thin "cracklin' crust" pizza dough to order for the brick oven. Live hickory-grilled meats, Bud's Red Hot Wings, and a kitchen open until 2 a.m. daily.
📍 1524 Clinton Hills Pkwy, Swansea, IL 62226

### Cholula's Mexican Restaurant
Cholula's is the town's go-to sit-down Mexican — guacamole made fresh in-house, enchiladas, fajitas, sizzling burritos, and a $1.49 Taco Tuesday that draws a crowd. Consistently ranked among Swansea's top restaurants.
📍 1500 N Illinois St, Swansea, IL 62226

### India's Oven
India's Oven is the long-running neighborhood Indian spot reviewers praise for warm service — butter chicken, garlic naan, tandoori breads, and Gobi Manchurian, most plates landing $10–$20. The reliable Indian.
📍 2625 N Illinois St, Swansea, IL 62226

### Soulcial Kitchen
Soulcial Kitchen is more than a restaurant — a chef-driven "hospitality campus" with a craft bar, dog park, and food-truck park, run by a team whose "Currency of Caring" program funds free meals for neighbors facing hunger. The Soulcial Smash Burger layers house pimento cheese over chow chow. Closed Sundays.
📍 127 N Belt E, Swansea, IL 62226

### Li Chinese Restaurant
Li Chinese is the family-owned Route 159 standby regulars credit for fresh ingredients, generous portions, and friendly counter service — General Tso's chicken and crab rangoon the easy orders. The dependable Chinese.
📍 2659 N Illinois St, Swansea, IL 62226

### Swansea Fish Stand
Swansea Fish Stand is a true local institution — open Fridays only, cash only — hand-breading cod, catfish, walleye, and bluegill in their own unique breading and frying it to order. Eat in or carry out. The whole charm is the one-day ritual.
📍 301 Service St, Swansea, IL 62226

If you want the most internationally delicious few blocks in St. Louis, you want Tower Grove. Anchored by the 289-acre Victorian Tower Grove Park, this guide spans Tower Grove East, Tower Grove South, and the area around the park including southern Shaw — and along six blocks of South Grand alone you'll find roughly 14 countries on the menu. It's affordable, eclectic, and minutes from downtown, which makes it a go-to for locals and the millions of out-of-towners in for a CITY SC soccer match, a Cardinals or Blues game, or a show at the Fox. From hand-scooped Ethiopian to liquid-nitrogen ice cream, here are 20 spots worth the trip.
Tower Grove dining splits into two main strips plus a cluster by the Garden: South Grand Blvd (the international row, east of the park, ~63118), Morgan Ford Rd (bars, bistros, brunch, in Tower Grove South 63116), and Shaw / 39th St by the Missouri Botanical Garden (63110). Most are independent and walkable; a few keep small hours, so call ahead. For neighborhood-level detail, see our Tower Grove East and Shaw neighborhood guides.

### Tee Rak Thai (Shaw / 39th St)
Northern Thai that graduated from a Tower Grove Farmers' Market stall to a storefront in 2026 — the khao soi (egg-noodle curry with a slow-cooked chicken leg, crispy noodles on top) is a mother's recipe.
📍 2203 S 39th St, St. Louis, MO 63110

### Five Aces Bar-B-Que (Shaw)
A neighborhood smokehouse near the Botanical Garden — baby back ribs, beef brisket, and weekend smoked wings.
📍 4000 Shaw Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63110

### Baileys' Range (Shaw)
Locally sourced burgers from well-known St. Louis restaurateur Dave Bailey — try "The Wake Up" (coffee rub, berry-black-pepper jam, bacon jam).
📍 4175 Shaw Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63110

### Ices Plain & Fancy (Shaw / 39th St)
Liquid-nitrogen ice cream flash-churned to order tableside in clouds of nitrogen — flavors like salted dulce de leche, with a speakeasy theme.
📍 2256 S 39th St, St. Louis, MO 63110

### Fiddlehead Fern Cafe (Shaw)
A tiny Shaw corner café known for from-scratch handmade croissants and avocado-and-tomato toasts.
📍 4066 Russell Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63110

### La Patisserie Chouquette (Shaw / Tower Grove Ave)
A boutique French patisserie from fine-dining-trained chef Simone Faure — flaky croissants, macarons, and cheesecakes near the Farmers' Market.
📍 1626 Tower Grove Ave, St. Louis, MO 63110

### Why this area matters
Tower Grove is the metro's most internationally delicious stretch — Ethiopian, Brazilian, Vietnamese, Thai, Lebanese, vegan Mexican, French pastry, St. Louis hot dogs, and nitrogen ice cream within walking distance of a Victorian park, all affordable and eclectic. It's why locals and out-of-towners alike land here before a CITY SC match, a Cardinals or Blues game, or a night at the Fox. More on-page than any chain app will ever surface.

### FAQ
What's the best area to eat in Tower Grove, St. Louis?
South Grand Blvd along the east edge of Tower Grove Park — six blocks with roughly 14 countries represented, the most internationally diverse dining strip in the metro. Morgan Ford Rd (Tower Grove South) adds bars, bistros, and brunch.
What are the must-try Tower Grove restaurants?
Meskerem (hand-eaten Ethiopian), Brasilia (most-authentic-in-STL Brazilian), Steve's Hot Dogs (the "official St. Louis" dog), Tee Rak Thai's khao soi, and Ices Plain & Fancy's liquid-nitrogen ice cream.
Is Tower Grove good before a CITY SC, Cardinals, or Blues game?
Yes — it sits just southwest of downtown, an easy drive to CITYPARK, Busch Stadium, Enterprise Center, and the Fox Theatre, which makes it a popular, affordable pre- and post-event dinner zone.
Is Tower Grove dining expensive?
No — it's known for affordable, eclectic international food. Many of the South Grand spots are $ to $$, from hot dogs and tacos to Ethiopian and Vietnamese.

Part of West County — explore the whole region in our West County restaurant guide .
Town and Country is one of West County's most affluent, almost entirely residential suburbs — so the food here is quality over quantity, clustered in a couple of upscale retail pockets. But what's here is genuinely good: a Sicilian fine-dining room that's done elaborate tableside service since 1972, a wood-fired pizza-and-pasta osteria, the West County outpost of a Clayton Italian institution, and a Vail-inspired neighborhood gastropub. Several spots people think are Town and Country are actually next door in Chesterfield, so we kept to the real city limits.
From 50-year tableside Sicilian to squid-ink black spaghetti, here's where to eat in Town and Country.
The restaurants live in two upscale strips — Town & Country Crossing (off Clayton/Mason near Hwy 40-141) and Lamp & Lantern Village / Woodsmill Plaza (63017). It's thin by design — this is residential West County — so for more range, neighboring Chesterfield, Frontenac, and Des Peres carry far more. A couple of "Town and Country" names (Gianfabio's, YaYa's) are actually Chesterfield.

### John Mineo's Italian Restaurant
The local legend. John Mineo's has served white-tablecloth Sicilian fine dining on Clayton Road since 1972 — opened by John Sr. and Anna Mineo, who emigrated from Palermo in 1959 — and it's one of the last St. Louis rooms still doing elaborate tableside presentations. Over 50 years, family-run.
📍 13490 Clayton Rd, Town and Country, MO 63131

### Katie's Pizza & Pasta Osteria
Katie's is chef Katie Collier's locally- and woman-owned wood-fired osteria — the squid-ink black spaghetti with seafood, the signature fried artichokes, and a screaming-hot brick oven charring the Margherita crust. Local, seasonal, scratch.
📍 14171 Clayton Rd, Town and Country, MO 63017

### Napoli 2
Napoli 2 is the West County outpost of Clayton's Café Napoli (owners Kathy and Tony) — dinner-only upscale Italian where the beef-filled toasted ravioli with homemade marinara is the St. Louis icon done right, alongside Gorgonzola arancini and veal piccata. The special-occasion table on this side of the county.
📍 1054 Town and Country Crossing Dr, Town and Country, MO 63017

### The Country Club Bar and Grill
The Country Club Bar and Grill is owner John Cain's cozy gastropub — he opened it in 1995 after living in Vail, aiming to bring that warm mountain-town tavern feel (fireplace, patio, easy regulars) to West County. Scratch-made American pub fare. Closed Sundays.
📍 288 Lamp and Lantern Village, Town and Country, MO 63017

### Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant
Cooper's Hawk is the Napa-style winery-and-restaurant with an in-house wine club and tasting room paired with upscale-casual New American food. It's a national chain (labeled honestly), but it's the splashy, very popular name in Town & Country Crossing.
📍 1146 Town and Country Crossing Dr, Town and Country, MO 63017

### Why this town matters
Town and Country is residential and upscale, so its dining is small but real — a 50-year tableside Sicilian legend, a chef-owned wood-fired osteria, a Clayton-institution outpost. The apps can't tell which spots are actually here versus next door in Chesterfield; we keep it honest and point you over the line for more.

### FAQ
What's the best restaurant in Town and Country, MO?
John Mineo's — Sicilian fine dining on Clayton Rd since 1972, one of the last St. Louis rooms still doing elaborate tableside presentations. For a chef-driven night, Katie's Pizza & Pasta.
Why is the dining scene small in Town and Country?
It's one of West County's most affluent, almost purely residential suburbs — restaurants cluster in a couple of upscale retail strips (Town & Country Crossing and Lamp & Lantern Village). Quality over quantity.
Are some "Town and Country" restaurants actually in Chesterfield?
Yes — Gianfabio's, YaYa's Euro Bistro, and Oaxaca all show up under Town and Country (sometimes sharing the 63017 ZIP) but are actually in Chesterfield. For more options, look one town over.
What's the local-vs-chain mix?
The genuine independents are John Mineo's, Katie's, Napoli 2, and The Country Club Bar and Grill; the big national name is Cooper's Hawk (a winery chain).

Here's a small-town surprise worth the drive east: Trenton, Illinois — a former coal town of about 2,700 people in Clinton County, named by a homesick settler after Trenton, New Jersey — keeps an honest-to-goodness food row. On and around Broadway , within a couple of walkable blocks, you'll find a Sinatra-era supper club, a hand-roasting coffee shop, homemade Mexican, and a family bowling alley that's been frying breakfast since 1967. For a town this size, that's a genuine "wait, all of this is still here?" moment.
That staying power is the whole story. Here's where to eat in Trenton.
The good news: nearly everything clusters on or just off Broadway , so park once and walk. The coffee shop is mornings-only and a couple of kitchens close Mondays, so check hours. Time it for TrentonFest (third weekend of August) and the city park fills with music, food, and rides. Want to extend the day? Hidden Lake Winery is just outside town.

### Trenton House
Start with the flagship. Trenton House is the town's supper club — warm, Sinatra-era room, upscale-but-affordable, doing seafood, pork chops, and steaks. The dress-up-a-little spot that proves a town of 2,700 can still keep a proper restaurant going.
📍 2 E Broadway St, Trenton, IL 62293

### Mexico on Main
Mexico on Main is the family-owned Mexican kitchen that cooks homemade, not prepackaged — chimichangas, enchiladas, and tacos that top the local rankings, with lively weekends and big margaritas.
📍 10 S Main St, Trenton, IL 62293

### Press Coffee & Tea
The mom-and-pop gem. Press Coffee & Tea hand-roasts its own coffee and curates local teas in a cozy Broadway storefront — fully customizable drinks and a genuine specialty-coffee program in a town you'd never expect to find one. Mornings only, and worth setting the alarm for.
📍 19 W Broadway, Trenton, IL 62293

### 7 West Bar & Grill
7 West is the downtown bar-and-grill with a big local following — homemade pizza , a deep beer list, Friday fish tacos, and weekend breakfast. The everyday Broadway hangout.
📍 7 W Broadway, Trenton, IL 62293

### Hank's Bowl Lounge & Restaurant
This is the one with the story. Hank's Bowl has been a family-run bowling lounge since 1967 — six lanes, a full bar, and a kitchen doing breakfast, lunch, and dinner (Taco Thursday, chicken wraps, burgers), plus live music. Bowl a game, eat a real meal, and soak up nearly sixty years of small-town history.
📍 29 W Illinois St, Trenton, IL 62293

### Pizza Market
Pizza Market is the independent pizzeria locals rely on for the everyday lunch buffet — pizzas, a big salad bar, and a fountain drink for a few bucks. The unfussy midday workhorse.
📍 111 W Broadway, Trenton, IL 62293

### Dairy King
And for the sweet finish, Dairy King is the classic independent ice-cream-and-burgers walk-up — frozen treats plus a full menu of breakfast, burgers, and takeout. The all-American cap to a Broadway crawl.
📍 320 W Broadway, Trenton, IL 62293

### Why this little town matters
A 2,700-person former coal town that still keeps a 1967 family bowling-alley diner, a hand-roasting coffee shop, a Sinatra-era supper club, and a homemade-pizza bar — all on the same Broadway block — is exactly the kind of "they're all still here" story the national apps will never tell you. They'll point you to the nearest interstate chain; they'll miss the entire downtown.

What's the best restaurant in Trenton, IL?
Trenton House, the town's supper club (seafood, steaks, pork chops) — the top full-service spot. For something more casual, 7 West Bar & Grill and Mexico on Main are local favorites.
What's the most unique place to eat in Trenton?
Hank's Bowl Lounge & Restaurant — a family-run bowling alley since 1967 with a full kitchen and bar. Bowl a game and get a real meal.

Press Coffee & Tea on Broadway — a mornings-only specialty shop that hand-roasts its own coffee and curates local teas.

The third weekend of August, at the city park — live music, food, drinks, and carnival rides, raising money for the Trenton Park Boosters.

Truesdale and Warrenton literally share the I-70 frontage (Highway M and Veterans Memorial Pkwy), so two spots a block apart can sit in different cities — and even different ZIPs (63380 vs Warrenton's 63383). The four below are Truesdale-side; for the fuller picture, see our Warrenton guide. A couple keep early or limited hours, so call ahead.

### Taquería el Tapanco de Don Chilo
The local favorite — a family-run taquería (in the former El Rincon space) where birria tacos draw a loyal following for their tender, savory depth, alongside chorizo street tacos and well-seasoned enchiladas. Homemade chips, salsa, and guac, with an outdoor deck and Mexican music playing inside.
📍 1020 E Veterans Memorial Pkwy, Truesdale, MO 63380

### MO' YUM Sandwich Co.
A gourmet sandwich shop whose whole pitch is "no boring sandwiches" — Boar's Head meats, house-made MO' YUM sauce, a strong Cuban and Buffalo Chicken, and any build available pressed, as a wrap, or as a salad. Filler-free meats and cane-sugar drinks.
📍 1032 E State Hwy M, Truesdale, MO 63380

### Olive's Bakery
The 5 a.m. bakery locals rave about — "the best donuts I have ever had in my life," big and fluffy, plus cinnamon rolls and pecan cinnamon rolls. Early morning Tue–Sat; get there before the case empties.
📍 902 E State Hwy M, Truesdale, MO 63380

### World Brew Cafe
A coffeehouse with a mission — run inside the Righteous Rides nonprofit, it's effectively donation-based, with featured-bean pour-overs and "coffee with a different worldview." Meeting rooms and free WiFi make it a genuine community hangout. Tue–Fri daytime.
📍 1440 E Veterans Memorial Pkwy, Truesdale, MO 63380

### Why this town matters
Truesdale is small and easy to lump in with Warrenton — but it has its own genuine I-70 strip: a birria taquería, a craft sandwich shop, a 5 a.m. donut bakery, and a mission coffeehouse, all locally owned. The apps mislabel which side of the line they're on; we keep Truesdale's own spots straight.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Imagine you've got a free Saturday and about an hour of daylight to burn. You point the car southwest out of St. Louis, the suburbs thin into rolling Franklin County farmland, and you land on a courthouse square that looks like it hasn't been in a hurry since 1923. You're hungry. And — pleasant surprise — you're in exactly the right place.
Union is the Franklin County seat, and like a lot of true county-seat towns, its food scene clusters where the town has always gathered: around the square and out along Highway 50. What you won't find much of here is the interchangeable national stuff. What you will find is a diner that's been at it for nearly ninety years, a margarita spot the whole town swears by, and a coffee roaster doing it the slow way. Here's where to eat in Union.

### White Rose Café
Start with the institution. The White Rose Café has been feeding Union for close to ninety years — a smoke-free, family-style diner a short walk from the courthouse, with a different home-cooked special every single day. This is the spot where the town's memory lives, one blue-plate at a time.
📍 208 E Main St, Union, MO 63084

### Que Pasa! Mexican Restaurant
Ask around the square about Friday night and someone will point you to Que Pasa! , just off the courthouse on S Oak Street. Locals are near-unanimous on two things: the frozen margaritas and the portions, both generous. Street-style carnitas quesadillas, Jalisco fajitas — it's the independent Mexican spot that's earned its loyalty.
📍 116 S Oak St, Union, MO 63084

### Dahlia Café
For a slower morning, Dahlia Café is the family-run brunch favorite on the east side of town. The breakfast chimichanga is the signature, but the Nutella-and-fresh-strawberry pancakes and the Supreme Scramble have their own fan clubs — and yes, there are mimosas and fresh-squeezed OJ.
📍 1595 Denmark Rd, Suite 4, Union, MO 63084

### Johnny's Restaurant
Some places are their owner, and Johnny's is one of them. Johnny got his start in restaurants at fifteen, bussing tables at a place called Merk's, worked his way up, earned a degree in Restaurant Hospitality, managed chain restaurants for years — and then, in 2001, bought a piece of land and built his own from the ground up in Union. Walk in today and you'll likely spot him behind the grill cooking your food himself; on a busy day you might even catch him bussing a table. That's the kind of owner-operated cooking the chains can't fake.
📍 1298 N Hwy 47, Union, MO 63084

### Junie Moon Café
Junie Moon Café is the homemade-meal, all-day kind of place — breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with fried shrimp and chicken doing the heavy lifting and beer, wine, and mimosas on offer. Early weekend hours (6 a.m. Saturday and Sunday) make it a go-to for the get-up-and-go crowd.
📍 340 W US Hwy 50, Union, MO 63084

### Hagie's 19 Bar & Grill
Some places are stitched right into the town's story. Hagie's 19 was opened back in 1987 by Steve Hagedorn to give Union the quality local bar it didn't have — and nearly forty years on, it's still the community's burger-and-wings hub, with half-pound patties, fried chicken, and a signature spicy wing sauce.
📍 618 N Washington Ave, Union, MO 63084

### Red, White & Brew Coffee Co.
For the caffeine, skip the drive-thru chains and head to Red, White & Brew , a Union independent roasting its own beans small-batch since 2017. A real master-roaster operation in a county-seat town — that's the kind of thing the big apps will never tell you about.
📍 317 US Hwy 50 West, Suite C, Union, MO 63084

### A county seat worth the drive
Union's whole downtown orbits the Franklin County Courthouse — built in 1922–23, on the National Register, with a Veterans Hall of Honor inside — and the food follows suit, gathering on E Main and S Oak by the square and out along Highway 50 . Time it right and you'll hit the Founder's Day Festival on the square the first Saturday in June, or the Franklin County Fair in mid-June, both reliably loaded with good food.
This is precisely the kind of town the national directories skim right over — which is the whole reason we built a local one. Search St Louis Near Me Directory for Union and Franklin County and you'll find the places worth your drive. (One honest note: for a winery or brewery night, you'll head to neighboring Washington or New Haven — Union's strength is its diners, its Mexican spot, and its coffee.)

### FAQ
What's the oldest restaurant in Union, MO?
The White Rose Café, which has served the town for nearly ninety years — about as close to a living landmark as a small-town diner gets.
Where do locals go for Mexican food in Union?
Que Pasa! on S Oak Street, just off the courthouse square, is the local favorite — known especially for its frozen margaritas and big portions.
Is there a true owner-operated restaurant in Union?
Johnny's Restaurant on N Hwy 47 — owner Johnny built the place himself in 2001 and still cooks behind the grill, exactly the kind of hands-on spot that defines a small town.
Are there wineries or breweries in Union?
Not inside the city itself — for that, the nearby Franklin County towns of Washington and New Haven are your best bet. Union's scene is built on diners, family cafés, and a great independent coffee roaster.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of St. Louis County — explore the whole region in our St. Louis County restaurant guide .
The Delmar Loop in University City isn't just a place to eat — it's where a huge slice of St. Louis food culture was born . Joe Edwards opened Blueberry Hill here in 1972 and sparked a revival that turned six blocks of Delmar into one of "America's 10 Great Streets," lined with the Walk of Fame's brass stars, the Tivoli Theatre, live-music halls, and a Chuck Berry statue. Several beloved St. Louis restaurant names got their start right on this strip.
From a root-beer bottling plant you can eat inside to Korean-Mexican tacos invented here, here's where to eat in University City.
This guide covers the University City (63130) side of the Loop — the western stretch with the U City Lions and City Hall. A few spots a block or two east are technically the St. Louis city side; we note those. Parking's easiest in the Loop garage. Time it for Loop in Motion (an October arts festival) or the January Loop Ice Carnival .

### Blueberry Hill
Start where the Loop started. Blueberry Hill is Joe Edwards's restaurant-bar-and-music-club, open since 1972 — burgers, a wall-to-wall pop-culture collection, and the downstairs Duck Room , where Chuck Berry played 209 monthly shows. The 8-foot Chuck Berry statue stands across the street. The anchor of the whole Loop.
📍 6504 Delmar Blvd, University City, MO 63130

### Fitz's
Fitz's is a family restaurant built around a working root-beer bottling plant — a 1940s-vintage line bottles soda behind glass while you eat. Burgers, root beer floats, and the house sodas you'll later find in groceries region-wide. A true St. Louis original.
📍 6605 Delmar Blvd, University City, MO 63130

### Salt + Smoke
Salt + Smoke is the original location of the now-beloved St. Louis BBQ name — brisket, ribs, the "white cheddar cracker" app, and a big bourbon list — right next to the Chuck Berry statue. A Loop original worth the smoke.
📍 6525 Delmar Blvd, University City, MO 63130

### Seoul Taco
Seoul Taco started as a 2011 food truck and built its home base here on the Loop — Korean-Mexican fusion (bulgogi tacos, the "Seoul bowl," kimchi fried rice) that grew into a regional name. The flavor was invented in St. Louis; this is where it lives.
📍 6665 Delmar Blvd, Ste 100A, University City, MO 63130

### Session Taco (formerly Mission Taco Joint)
The Loop's first Session Taco — recently renamed from Mission Taco Joint — does West-Coast-style street tacos, margaritas, and craft beer. This 2013 spot was the original of another St. Louis-grown favorite. (Heads-up: if your map still says "Mission Taco Joint," it's the same place.)
📍 6235 Delmar Blvd, University City, MO 63130

### Ranoush
Ranoush brings Syrian and Middle Eastern cooking to the Loop — mezze, shawarma, kebabs, and falafel from family recipes. A genuinely good independent for a sit-down Mediterranean meal.
📍 6501 Delmar Blvd, University City, MO 63130

### Three Kings Public House
Three Kings is the Loop gastropub — smash burgers, Cajun pasta, wings, and 30-plus rotating craft taps. After a 2023 fire, the community rallied and it reopened bigger one door west, with patio seating on Delmar. A comeback story with a great beer list.
📍 6315 Delmar Blvd, University City, MO 63130

### Just east on the Loop (St. Louis city side)
A couple of standouts sit a block or two east, technically on the St. Louis city side of Delmar: Eclipse atop the boutique Moonrise Hotel (rooftop dining, also a Joe Edwards project) and Nudo House (ramen, pho, bánh mì). Same Loop stroll, just over the line.

### Why this little town matters
The Delmar Loop is living proof of the directory's whole idea: dig into a real local strip and you find the origins of a food scene — Blueberry Hill's 1972 revival, Fitz's bottling line, the first Salt + Smoke, the trucks-turned-icons Seoul Taco and Session Taco. The national apps list them flat; the real story is that they all started on this one street.

### FAQ
What restaurants started on the Delmar Loop?
Several St. Louis favorites began here: Blueberry Hill (1972), the original Salt + Smoke, Seoul Taco (from a 2011 food truck), and Session Taco (the original Mission Taco Joint, 2013).
Is it Mission Taco Joint or Session Taco?
The Loop location recently rebranded from Mission Taco Joint to Session Taco — same spot, new name (your map may still show the old one).
What's there to do on the Loop besides eat?
The St. Louis Walk of Fame (150+ brass stars in the sidewalk), the Chuck Berry statue, the Tivoli Theatre, Blueberry Hill's Duck Room, and the Pageant/Delmar Hall music venues.
Which Loop spots are actually in University City?
Blueberry Hill, Fitz's, Salt + Smoke, Seoul Taco, Ranoush, and Three Kings are on the University City (63130) side; a few east-end spots (Eclipse, Nudo House) are the St. Louis city side of Delmar.

A burger at Blueberry Hill, a root beer float at Fitz's, brisket at Salt + Smoke, and a stroll past the Walk of Fame. For more local spots across the metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Part of West County — explore the whole region in our West County restaurant guide .
Valley Park is one of those St. Louis County towns you've driven past a hundred times on the way to Castlewood or Six Flags without ever stopping. Pull off and you'll find a real river town — built on the north bank of the Meramec , flooded and rebuilt more than once, now tucked safe behind a levee — with an old downtown by the water and a food scene that's almost entirely mom-and-pop.
This is a town with stories: a diner that's been family-run since 1954, a Mexican family that's fed the place for thirty years across two restaurants, and a convenience store down by the levee that's secretly slinging real New Orleans cooking next to the live bait. Here's where to eat in Valley Park.
The food here clusters in two pockets — the Meramec Station / Stonegate retail strip up by the highway, and old downtown along St. Louis Avenue near the river and the levee. The downtown river pair is where the town's character lives. A couple of spots close Mondays, and the levee-side kitchens keep their own hours, so a quick check before you go never hurts.

### Young's Restaurant & Ice Creamery
Start at the oldest. Young's has been a family-owned diner and homemade ice creamery since 1954 — burgers, plate lunches, and a frozen-custard-and-ice-cream window that's fed three generations of Valley Park. It's the town's living room, and the kind of place a chain can only imitate.
📍 206 Meramec Station Rd, Valley Park, MO 63088

### El Nopal Mexican Restaurant
Here's the family at the heart of it. The Cortez family has run El Nopal in Valley Park for roughly thirty years — a sit-down Mexican spot known for big portions and fresh plates, and the anchor of a genuine local food legacy.
📍 3 Stonegate Ctr, Valley Park, MO 63088

### El Jarocho Mexican Store & Taqueria
Then, in 2021, the same Cortez family opened a second concept a few doors down: El Jarocho , a Mexican grocery and taqueria doing street tacos and all-day breakfast burritos. The barbacoa and lengua tacos are the standouts — they pay up for better meat, and you can taste it. Two restaurants, one family, three decades of feeding this town.
📍 25 Stonegate Ctr, Valley Park, MO 63088

### Asian Corner
Asian Corner quietly earned the title of "Best Asian Restaurant in the St. Louis Metro" from a regional review outlet in 2024 — a family-owned Thai-and-pan-Asian kitchen turning out pad Thai and house fried rice that pull people in from well outside Valley Park. Closed Mondays; worth planning around.
📍 204 Meramec Valley Plaza, Valley Park, MO 63088

### Troy Mediterranean Cuisine
For gyros, shawarma, falafel, and a hummus worth the trip, Troy Mediterranean has been a family-owned fixture in the Stonegate strip since 2014 — the head chef brought 15-plus years of experience to it, and it shows. Dine in, carry out, or feed a crowd.
📍 19 Stonegate Ctr, Valley Park, MO 63088

### Meramec Jack's
Down in old downtown by the levee, Meramec Jack's is the family-owned bar and grill named for the river itself — burgers, pizza, a little BBQ, and a late-night kitchen running till the early hours. This is the riverfront-town tavern, the spot that feels like Valley Park's actual front porch.
📍 100 St Louis Ave, Valley Park, MO 63088

### Duck In Market
And now the one you won't believe until you go: Duck In Market is a convenience store and bait shop — lottery, ice, live worms — with a full Cajun and New Orleans kitchen running inside it. Get your tackle for the Meramec and a real po'boy in the same stop. It's the most river-town thing in any river town, and it's delicious.
📍 324 St Louis Ave, Valley Park, MO 63088

### Make it a day: Mackenzie Brewing & the Meramec
Valley Park has its own small-batch brewery, Mackenzie Brewing Co. (932 Meramec Station Rd), pouring Belgian-style beers — call ahead, as the taproom's status has wavered. Pair a meal with a paddle or hike: Castlewood State Park is minutes west on Big Bend, and the Meramec itself runs right through town. Eat, drink, and get on the water.

### Why this little town matters
Valley Park keeps getting written off as a highway exit, but the truth is it's a river town with a memory — flooded and rebuilt, leveed and stubborn, with a 1954 diner, a 30-year Mexican family running two restaurants, a metro-best Asian kitchen, and a bait shop slinging gumbo down by the water. The national apps can't see any of that. They show you logos; they miss the town.

### FAQ
What's the oldest restaurant in Valley Park, MO?
Young's Restaurant & Ice Creamery, family-owned since 1954 — a diner-and-ice-cream institution and about as close to a town landmark as a meal gets.
Where do locals go for Mexican food in Valley Park?
The Cortez family's two spots: El Nopal (sit-down, ~30 years in town) and El Jarocho (a newer taqueria and Mexican grocery known for barbacoa and lengua tacos).
What's the most unusual place to eat in Valley Park?
Duck In Market — a convenience store and live-bait shop downtown that runs a full Cajun/New Orleans kitchen inside. Tackle and a po'boy in one stop.
Is there anything to do in Valley Park besides eat?
Plenty — Castlewood State Park for hiking and the bluffs is minutes away, the Meramec River runs through town for paddling and fishing, and Mackenzie Brewing pours small-batch beer (call ahead for hours).

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Venice is a tiny, deeply historic Mississippi River town across from north St. Louis — it peaked at over 6,000 residents in 1950 and has since shrunk to around 1,450, with nearly one in five homes vacant. So it's remarkable that Venice still has two genuine, locally owned, Black-owned eateries inside its limits — and both are beloved local institutions, not just options. People in Venice get hungry too — here are the real spots, plus where to go nearby.
From hand-dipped shakes at an old-school drive-in to catfish a reviewer called "fire," here's where to eat in Venice.
Venice's two spots are on Broadway and Lincoln St (62090), anchored near the McKinley Bridge with Illinois Route 3 running through. Both are small operations with limited days/hours — call ahead. Disambiguation: many "Venice" results are really Granite City (Big Meechie's, Teri's, Jacobsmeyer's) — those have their own Granite City guide. ### John's Drive-In
A genuine old-school neighborhood drive-in that's outlasted the town around it — burgers, wings, fries, hand-dipped shakes, and slushes from a family-run window. The kind of community staple that's been a Venice fixture for decades.
📍 417 Broadway, Venice, IL 62090

### Niddy's Kitchen
The catfish destination — a Black-owned soul-food and Southern-comfort kitchen (also breakfast, brunch, and seafood) where one reviewer's verdict on the catfish was simply "it was fire... a must have." Ranked among Venice's top spots, with fried chicken and tacos rounding it out. Small operation, limited days — call ahead.
📍 401 Lincoln St, Venice, IL 62090

### Closest spots a short drive away
Venice is small and hemmed in by neighbors, so backup eats are a minute or two away:
- Mill's Place — south in Brooklyn (Lovejoy) — real-deal soul food and big plate-lunches with twice-monthly Soul Food Sundays (see our Brooklyn guide).
- Perigen Tavern — north in Madison — a friendly neighborhood tavern (see our Madison guide).

### Why this town matters
Venice is one of the most depopulated towns in the metro — which makes its two surviving, Black-owned institutions all the more worth celebrating, not overlooking. A decades-old drive-in and a catfish kitchen that locals swear by: that's the real Venice, and nobody else maps it honestly. We do.

What's the best place to eat in Venice, IL?
Niddy's Kitchen on Lincoln St — a Black-owned soul-food kitchen whose catfish gets rave local reviews. For a classic burger-and-shake, John's Drive-In on Broadway. Both are small, locally owned, and beloved.
Why are there so few restaurants in Venice?
Venice lost about three-quarters of its population since 1950 (from over 6,000 to ~1,450), so a town that small can't sustain many restaurants — which is exactly why its two survivors are treasured local institutions.

Vinita Park is a small 0.72-square-mile residential triangle of about 1,800 people, just south of St. Charles Rock Road and east of I-170. For years it had essentially no dining — but as of 2026 there's a forearm-sized burrito drive-through inside the limits and an award-winning West African kitchen right on the line. People here get hungry too — here's what's real in town, plus the closest spots a few minutes out.
From a 1 a.m. one-pound burrito to a TV-champion oxtail stew, here's where to eat in Vinita Park.

### Abelardo's Mexican Fresh
The in-limits spot — a Southern-California-style Mexican drive-through in a converted Jack in the Box, running 7 a.m. to 3 a.m. One-pound burritos rolled in 14-inch shells, beef fried tacos five-for-$5.99 on Taco Tuesdays. The move when it's late and you want a fresh, scratch-made burrito the size of your forearm. (Drive-through only.)
📍 8307 Page Blvd, Vinita Park, MO 63114

### FUFU n' Sauce (right on the Vinita Park line)
A standout West African (Togolese) kitchen that grew from a food truck — owner-chef Adjo Honsou won Season 3 of PBS's "The Great American Recipe." The Oxtail Palm Nut Stew is the flagship (the oxtail starts in a pressure cooker so the spice runs all the way through), alongside goat pepper soup, egusi, jollof, and fufu. Sits right on the Vinita Park / University City line on Page.
📍 8100 Page Ave, MO (Vinita Park / University City line)

### Charlack Pub (Charlack)
A beloved neighborhood bar in tiny Charlack, minutes away — known for near-nightly live music and jams (hosted by Judy) and a Friday-night taco bar. Come for the drinks, music, and Friday tacos.
📍 8334 Lackland Rd, Charlack, MO 63114

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
You're an hour west of the city on I-70, the strip malls have thinned into rolling Warren County farmland, and you pull off at Warrenton because you're hungry and the gas-station hot dog is not happening. Here's the good news: you've landed on the old Boone's Lick Road — the actual westward trail Daniel Boone's sons cut through here — and the town that grew up along it still feeds people like it means it.
Most folks blow past Warrenton on the way to the Lake of the Ozarks or Missouri wine country. Their loss. Behind the outlet-mall signs is a real food town: a veteran-owned smokehouse, a scratch diner that bans frozen food, a Mexican cantina the whole county claims, and even a winery serving seafood boils right downtown. Here's where to eat before you get back on the interstate.
Warrenton is the Warren County seat , so a lot of life still orbits the courthouse and the old downtown along Booneslick Road, while the newer spots cluster out by the highway and the outlet shops. A few of these keep small-town hours (early-close bakeries, weekend-only winery kitchens) — a quick call before you drive saves a sad parking-lot U-turn. Time it for FrühlingFest in June and you'll catch the town's German heritage spilling into the streets.

### Hwy 47 Kitchen
Start where the locals start their mornings. Hwy 47 Kitchen cooks everything fresh — "no shortcuts, no frozen items" is practically the house motto — and it shows in the biscuits and gravy, the hot chicken sandwich, and a cheeseburger that tastes like somebody actually stood at the griddle for it. Breakfast and lunch only, with a drive-thru for the days you can't sit still.
📍 703 Warrior Ave, Warrenton, MO 63383

### Two Dudes Barbeque
Some BBQ joints are a brand. This one's a family. Two Dudes Barbeque is family-owned and veteran-owned, smoking locally sourced pork and beef low and slow in a small-town shack that earns its smoke ring the honest way. This is the kind of mom-and-pop the apps barely list and the regulars never shut up about.
📍 612 N Hwy 47, Warrenton, MO 63383

### Casa Tequila Cantina & Grill
Ask around about Mexican in Warrenton and you'll keep hearing the same name. Casa Tequila does birria tacos, trash-can nachos, big plates, and margaritas with conviction — an independent cantina, not a chain wearing a sombrero. Locals call it their favorite, and the portions back up the loyalty.
📍 1000 Warrenton Outlet Center, Ste 14, Warrenton, MO 63383

### Social House 227
Downtown's newer star, Social House 227 is the bright, modern gastropub the old Booneslick corridor needed — "kitchen sink" pizzas, the Comeback Burger, Philly steak sandwiches, live music, and a patio. It's the spot that makes a weeknight downtown feel like a night out.
📍 227 E Booneslick Rd, Warrenton, MO 63383

### The Hideout
Don't let the dive-bar look fool you — The Hideout quietly turns out some of the best plates in town. The fried chicken and the catfish dinner are the moves, with a french dip and a fried pork tenderloin for backup. It's the everybody-knows-your-name kind of place, which is exactly why the food's better than it has any right to be.
📍 405 W Veterans Memorial Pkwy, Warrenton, MO 63383

### Hometown Bakery
For the sweet stop, Hometown Bakery is the independent counter to hit early — cherry cake doughnuts, gooey butter cake (that St. Louis-region birthright), cakes and cupcakes, plus real coffee and specialty teas. Get there in the morning or the good stuff is gone; bakers don't wait around.
📍 902 State Hwy M, Ste A, Warrenton, MO 63383

### MK Ranch Bar & Grill
Here's one with a genuine hook: MK Ranch Bar & Grill is tied to a working Longhorn cattle ranch , so the steaks come with a backstory most steakhouses can only fake. Add truffle fries, live music, line dancing, and a little karaoke, and it's less a meal than an evening.
📍 1000 Warrenton Shoppes, Warrenton, MO 63383

### Hopewell Winery (Warrenton tasting room)
You don't expect a winery downtown , but Hopewell Winery put a tasting room right on the historic Boone's Lick Road — dry and sweet fruit-and-grape wines plus a real kitchen turning out seafood boils , soups, sandwiches, and pasta, with live music on the patio. It's the easy "stay a while" cap to a Warrenton afternoon — and a head start on the wine country just down the road.
📍 209 E Booneslick Rd, Warrenton, MO 63383

### Why this little town matters
Warrenton sits at a crossroads most people only ever drive through — the I-70 corridor laid right over the old Boone's Lick Road, the literal on-ramp from St. Louis to Missouri wine country. But pull off the highway and you'll find a county-seat town with a veteran-owned smokehouse, a scratch diner, a ranch-to-table grill, and a downtown winery, all locally owned. That's the kind of find the big review sites flatten to a list of fast-food exits.

Yes — it's about an hour out on I-70, and you can eat genuinely well here, from a scratch diner to a veteran-owned BBQ shack to a downtown winery. It beats another interstate fast-food stop every time.

Casa Tequila Cantina & Grill, out by the outlet center — an independent spot known for birria tacos, big portions, and strong margaritas.
Does Warrenton have a winery?
Yes — Hopewell Winery runs a tasting room right downtown on Booneslick Road, with fruit and grape wines and a full food menu including seafood boils. It's also the gateway to the larger Missouri wine country (Augusta, Defiance, Dutzow) a short drive south.
What's the food connection to Daniel Boone?
Warrenton grew up along the historic Boone's Lick Road — the westward trail blazed by Daniel Boone's sons. Downtown's main drag is literally still called Booneslick Road, and several of the best spots sit right on it.

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Washington is the rare river town that kept everything that makes a river town worth visiting — an intact brick downtown stepping down to the Missouri River, deep German roots, and a title nobody can take from it: Corn Cob Pipe Capital of the World , home of the Missouri Meerschaum Company, making corncob pipes since 1869. It's the unofficial heart of Missouri wine country, and its food-and-drink scene has grown to match.
This is a genuine destination downtown — a 1930 diner with mile-high pies, a fine-dining room in an 1839 mansion, a riverfront brewery, a distillery, and more. Here's where to eat in Washington.
The good stuff concentrates downtown along Front, Elm, Main, and 5th Streets , walkable and right by the river. Some of the best spots are newer (a 2025 brewery, a mansion restaurant) — confirm hours. Time it for the Washington Town & Country Fair in early August, one of the region's biggest, or come any weekend for the wine-country day-trip.

### Cowan's Restaurant
Start at the legend. Cowan's has been Washington's diner since 1930 (the "Cowan's" name since 1973) — famous for mile-high meringue pies and fried chicken, and still the place locals meet for breakfast. The oldest restaurant in town and its living room.
📍 114 Elm St, Washington, MO 63090

### Old Dutch Hotel & Tavern
The Old Dutch is the historic riverfront tavern (in a circa-1923 building with original pressed-tin ceilings), reimagined as a full-service tavern with a boutique hotel upstairs. Old-tavern charm, kept intact.
📍 227 Elm St, Washington, MO 63090

### Mangia Bella at Elijah McLean's
For the special occasion, Mangia Bella sets Italian-leaning fine dining inside the 1839 Elijah McLean mansion — 15,000 square feet of American Colonial history, family-owned, steaks and pasta and seafood. The dress-up dinner with a story.
📍 600 W Front St, Washington, MO 63090

### Oak & Front | Kitchen + Bar
Oak & Front is the upscale riverfront kitchen and wine-and-cocktail bar — modern American with a big river-view patio and Sunday brunch. The sophisticated downtown pick right on the bank of the Missouri.
📍 120 W Front St, Ste 201, Washington, MO 63090

### Marquart's Landing
For the casual riverfront night, Marquart's Landing is the locally beloved bar-and-grill known for "legendary" pizzas and Landing Burgers, with daily specials. The unfussy waterfront hang.
📍 300 W Front St, Washington, MO 63090

### The Washington Coffee Shop
The Washington Coffee Shop is the downtown coffee-and-breakfast spot in the historic Lefmann & Sons building — espresso, baked goods, breakfast, and lunch, seven days a week. (For a second option, underGROUNDS Espresso Bar on Front Street is also independent and well-loved.)
📍 2 E 5th St, Washington, MO 63090

### Birdie's Bakeshop
Birdie's is the small-batch independent bakery — jumbo cinnamon rolls, decorated shortbread, gooey butter cake, with notable alpha-gal-safe, vegan, and gluten-free options that make it a genuine find for restricted diets.
📍 116 W Front St, Ste 100, Washington, MO 63090

### Old Bridgeview Brewing
The newest reason to linger: Old Bridgeview Brewing opened in summer 2025 as a riverfront nano-brewery with locally sourced beers and pub-style food, billing itself "Missouri's first community brewery." It hosts an Oktoberfest, fitting for this German town.
📍 16 E Front St, Washington, MO 63090

### The Washington Distilling Co.
And to round it out, The Washington Distilling Co. makes small-batch bourbon, whiskey, and vodka with a tasting room downtown — the spirits side of a town that takes its drinks seriously.
📍 622 Jefferson St, Washington, MO 63090

### Why this little town matters
Washington is what a Missouri River town can be when it keeps its history: a 1930 diner, an 1839-mansion restaurant, a 1923 tavern, a riverfront brewery, a distillery, and the world's last great corncob-pipe factory, all in a walkable brick downtown at the heart of wine country. The national apps will route you to a chain on the highway and miss the whole river.

What's the oldest restaurant in Washington, MO?
Cowan's Restaurant, a downtown diner since 1930, famous for its mile-high meringue pies and fried chicken.
What is Washington, MO known for?
It's the "Corn Cob Pipe Capital of the World" — home of the Missouri Meerschaum Company, making corncob pipes since 1869 — and a historic Missouri River town at the heart of Missouri wine country.

Yes — Old Bridgeview Brewing (a riverfront nano-brewery that opened in 2025) and The Washington Distilling Co. (small-batch bourbon, whiskey, and vodka with a downtown tasting room).

By Lane Forman , Founder of St Louis Near Me Directory Local restaurant guides, researched and maintained · Updated June 2026 
Waterloo is the Monroe County seat — a German-rooted courthouse town on the Illinois bluffs, about 25 minutes southeast of downtown St. Louis. It started as the French settlement of Bellefontaine in the 1700s, then filled with German immigrants after the 1840s, and that heritage still flavors everything: the courthouse square, the old Peterstown House on the Kaskaskia–Cahokia trail, and a downtown that now boasts two craft breweries.
For a town of 11,000, Waterloo eats and drinks like a destination. Here's where to go.
The good stuff clusters downtown around the courthouse square and Main Street , with a couple of spots (Dreamland Palace, Schorr Lake) a few miles out but still in town. Several spots keep limited days, so check first. Time it for Mayfest (first Saturday in May) or the Monroe County Fair in late July.

### Stubborn German Brewing Company
Start with the namesake heritage. Stubborn German brews German and American styles in a restored 1885 dry-goods store downtown — 18 taps, a serious bourbon collection, and a rentable basement speakeasy. Its year-round Märzen, "Stubbornfest," is the move. Locally owned by the Rahns.
📍 119 S Main St, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Hopskeller Brewing Company
Two blocks over, Hopskeller is the 10-barrel brewpub in an 1850s former home — English- and Pacific-Northwest-influenced ales, wood-fired pizzas, brats, and small plates. Its Raspberry Wheat is the flagship, and it's racked up regional "best of" awards. Two real breweries in one small downtown is its own kind of flex.
📍 116 E 3rd St, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Dreamland Palace German Restaurant
For the real German feast, Dreamland Palace is the town's heritage anchor — authentic German and American plates from family recipes, lovingly restored by the Langs since 1990. A few miles out on Route 156, weekend-focused, and worth the drive.
📍 3043 State Route 156, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Zera Artisan Bakery & Cafe
The newest gem: Zera opened in 2025 inside the historic former Commercial State Bank building downtown — artisan breads, pastries, bagels, croissants, sandwiches, and good coffee in a relaxed, upscale room. The morning-and-lunch stop.
📍 101 S Main St, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Shorty's Smokehouse
Shorty's is the small-town low-and-slow BBQ spot right downtown, next to Stubborn German — the smoke to go with all that beer. Open seven days.
📍 121 S Main St, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Casa Romero Mexican Restaurant
Casa Romero is the family-friendly authentic Mexican spot — a hacienda-style room and a loyal local crowd, the dependable taco-and-margarita pick in town.
📍 512 S Market St, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Schorr Lake Vineyards & Winery
For a glass, Schorr Lake is the estate winery just south of town — table and fruit wines on a deck overlooking a six-acre vineyard and lake. The relaxed wine-country cap to a Waterloo afternoon.
📍 1032 S Library St, Waterloo, IL 62298

### Ahne's Bakery
And a nostalgic note: Ahne's Bakery — a family bakery since 1973, famous for gooey butter cake — lost its storefront to a 2022 fire but came back in 2025 as a limited pop-up (currently inside the Philly Pretzel Factory a couple of days a week). Confirm the current schedule, but the gooey butter is worth chasing down.
📍 (pop-up — confirm current location), Waterloo, IL 62298

### Why this little town matters
Waterloo is a 250-year-old German courthouse town that most St. Louisans have never explored — and it quietly fields two craft breweries, an authentic German restaurant, a 2025 artisan bakery, a downtown smokehouse, and an estate winery, all wrapped around a historic square. That's a destination downtown the national apps reduce to a few stray listings.
Search St Louis Near Me Directory for Waterloo and Monroe County before you go — and our Columbia guide (the next Monroe County town north) and Millstadt guide make an easy German-heritage trail.
And if you run a Waterloo spot — a brewery, a bakery, a food truck — a listing is how the next visitor to the square finds you .

### FAQ
Does Waterloo, IL have craft breweries?
Yes — two downtown: Stubborn German Brewing (in an 1885 building, with a basement speakeasy) and Hopskeller Brewing (a brewpub with wood-fired pizza in an 1850s home).
Where can I get authentic German food in Waterloo?
Dreamland Palace German Restaurant on Route 156 — family recipes, restored and run by the Langs since 1990. The whole town's German heritage runs deep.
What's the newest spot in Waterloo?
Zera Artisan Bakery & Cafe, opened in 2025 in the historic former Commercial State Bank building downtown — artisan breads, pastries, and coffee.
Is there a winery in Waterloo?
Yes — Schorr Lake Vineyards & Winery, an estate winery just south of town with a deck over a six-acre vineyard and lake.

A flight at Stubborn German, wood-fired pizza at Hopskeller, a German feast at Dreamland Palace, and a glass at Schorr Lake. For more local spots across Monroe County and the St. Louis metro, explore St Louis Near Me Directory .
